title: Anthropic struggles to secure cloud compute as providers view it as competitor
content: Anthropic is reportedly facing difficulties securing sufficient compute resources from cloud providers who increasingly perceive the company as a competitor. These challenges arise while Anthropic’s infrastructure expenditures continue to rise in anticipation of a planned stock market debut in November.
summary: Anthropic is reportedly struggling to secure enough compute from cloud providers that increasingly view it as a competitor. Its infrastructure spending is ballooning ahead of a planned November IPO.
author: TechCrunch

title: Hugging Face co‑founder Clem Delangue says Netflix’s “AI Gone Rogue” is inaccurate
content: Before you share the Netflix documentary "AI Gone Rogue" take note. Clem Delangue, Hugging Face's co-founder who is featured in the film, says it went "full doomer mode" and isn't accurate.
summary: Hugging Face co‑founder Clem Delangue says Netflix’s “AI Gone Rogue” is inaccurate.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic proposes AI safety bill requiring judge approval to block model release
content: Anthropic has proposed an AI safety bill that would permit blocking a model if it poses a risk of killing 50 or more people. However, the policy restricts federal agencies from halting a model’s release without first obtaining a judge’s permission, potentially limiting executive oversight in favor of judicial review.
summary: The proposed policy includes protections against dangerous AI but forbids federal agencies from blocking a model's release without a judge's permission. The bill may block a model if 50 or more people could be killed.
author: TechCrunch

title: Russia woos Asian tourists in attempt to counter European visits collapse
content: EU tourist arrivals to Russia dropped from 5 million in 2019 to 160,000 in 2025. This decline resulted from sanctions, cancelled flights, and other restrictions linked to Russia’s ongoing war in Ukraine, which severed Western leisure travel. Consequently, Moscow is actively courting Asian tourists to counter the collapse in European visits.
summary: Russia woos Asian tourists in attempt to counter European visits collapse.
author: Euronews

title: Lula supporters spell name in Rio waters before Brazil runoff
content: Lula supporters spelled out his name in Rio waters ahead of the Brazilian runoff election. The race remains tight, with polls showing a 51–49 lead. Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro recently clashed in a debate focusing on public spending, corruption, and ties to the US.
summary: Lula supporters spelled his name in Rio waters ahead of the Brazil runoff. The content notes a tense debate between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro over public spending, corruption, and US ties, with polls showing a tight 51–49 race.
author: Euronews

title: Two dead as heavy rain floods eastern Spain, submerging Valencia streets
content: Heavy rain in eastern Spain caused severe flooding, killing at least two people. In the Valencia region, streets and cars were submerged while rescuers evacuated stranded residents. Authorities urged residents to stay indoors amid the ongoing flood conditions.
summary: At least two people have died after heavy rain triggered flooding in eastern Spain. Streets and cars were submerged in the Valencia region as rescuers evacuated stranded residents.
author: Euronews

title: US Issues Rare Red Alert for Citizens in 12 Middle East Countries
content: Washington has issued a rare red alert to US citizens in 12 Middle Eastern countries. The warning cites risks of potential attacks on US interests in the region.
summary: Washington issued a rare red alert to US citizens in 12 Middle East countries. The alert cites risks of potential attacks on US interests.
author: Euronews

title: Italy deploys 500 troops to Milan and tightens security laws after clashes
content: Italy on Tuesday approved the deployment of 500 troops to Milan after violent clashes as fuel price protests hit pasta production and food deliveries in southern Italy. A cabinet meeting on Tuesday also approved a series of security measures, including making the detention of minors easier and introducing the crime of "violent participation in a demonstration". FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta reports from Rome.
summary: Italy approved sending 500 troops to Milan after violent clashes linked to fuel price protests that disrupted pasta production and food deliveries in southern Italy. The cabinet also approved security measures that make detaining minors easier and create a new offense for violent participation in a demonstration.
author: France 24

title: Trump Campaigns in Republican Strongholds as GOP Support Slides in Polls
content: US President Donald Trump is campaigning for Republican candidates in states he won by double digits in 2024, as midterm elections approach. According to France 24, this activity signals concerns within the party, as polls indicate a significant decline in GOP support, even in deep red states.
summary: US President Donald Trump is campaigning for Republican candidates in states he won by double digits in 2024 as the midterm elections approach, according to FRANCE 24's Monte Francis. Polls indicate that GOP support is slipping drastically, even in some deep red states.
author: France 24

title: Paris street medic alive after viral police beating video
content:
A video of French riot police violently beating a 26‑year‑old street medic in Paris has gone viral, prompting social media users to claim the medic died from his injuries. Those claims are untrue. The medic is alive and was interviewed by FRANCE 24.

The rumor spread because it was confused with a separate incident that occurred the same day in the same area. A man died of cardiac arrest there, and online users mistakenly conflated the two events. Vedika Bahl explains this mix‑up in the Truth or Fake segment.
summary: A video showing French riot police violently beating a 26-year-old street medic in Paris has gone viral, with social media users falsely claiming he died from his injuries. But the street medic is alive, and spoke to FRANCE 24.
author: France 24

title: US regulators certify Boeing 737 Max 10 after years of delay
content:
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration has granted final approval for Boeing’s 737‑10, the largest aircraft in the company’s best‑selling Max family. The certification arrives more than five years after the jet’s maiden flight and is described as an important step for Boeing, which has been working to regain momentum following a safety and management crisis.

Separately, the French government announced that it will offer an interest‑free loan of up to 50,000 euros to all businesses affected by recent riots.
summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration has given final approval for the 737-10, the largest model in Boeing's best-selling Max family. The certification comes more than five years after the narrowbody jet's maiden flight, and marks an important step for the planemaker that's been trying to regain ground following a safety and management crisis.
author: France 24

title: Lula Campaign to Disqualify Bolsonaro Over Alleged Meta Interference
content: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign is preparing to file a petition with Brazil’s top electoral court to annul the candidacy of right‑wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro. The request follows claims that the U.S. tech company Meta engaged in algorithmic manipulation, suppressing content from Lula’s campaign while boosting Bolsonaro’s. The lawsuit comes as the presidential race heads into a Sunday runoff, with Lula’s team arguing that Meta’s interference unfairly advantaged Bolsonaro in the election.
summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign is preparing to file a petition to annul Flavio Bolsonaro’s candidacy. The petition alleges that Meta’s algorithmic manipulation suppressed Lula’s campaign content and boosted Bolsonaro’s ahead of the Sunday runoff.
author: France 24

title: PSG End Barcelona's Winning Run with 4-2 Victory
content: Paris Saint‑Germain overturned a deficit to defeat Barcelona 4‑2 in a Champions League thriller on Tuesday, giving the Catalans their first loss of the season. Liverpool staged a dramatic comeback to win 4‑3 over Villarreal at Anfield. Manchester City secured a 5‑1 victory against AEK Athens.
summary: Paris Saint‑Germain beat Barcelona 4‑2, handing the Catalans their first defeat of the season. Liverpool edged Villarreal 4‑3 at Anfield while Manchester City won 5‑1 over AEK Athens.
author: France 24

title: Egypt's parliament delays debate on Sisi request for Saudi military support
content: Egypt's parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week, state media reported, after an emergency session ended without a decision a day earlier. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Dr May Darwich, Associate Professor in International Relations of the Middle East at the University of Birmingham. She explains that "this kind of military operation does not really have any objectives or exit strategy so at the moment this might actually weaken Egypt's regional role".
summary: Egypt's parliament postponed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al‑Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week. Dr May Darwich, Associate Professor in International Relations of the Middle East at the University of Birmingham, said the operation could weaken Egypt's regional role.
author: France 24

title: Nigeria Reports First Ebola Case in Abuja
content: Nigeria has reported its first known Ebola case amid Africa's latest outbreak that began in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said the patient, a woman, had recently flown to Abuja from Uganda.
summary: Nigeria has reported its first known case of Ebola during Africa's latest outbreak originating in the DRC. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said the patient was a woman who had recently flown to Abuja from Uganda.
author: DW World

title: Yemen war continues to force families from homes amid hunger and disease
content: The UN reports that more than 250,000 people have fled renewed fighting in Yemen. It cites particular concern for those sheltering in the southwestern city of Taiz and the wider governorate, where access is essentially blocked.
summary: Yemen war continues to force families from homes amid hunger and disease.
author: UN News

title: UNICEF chief urges end to child marriage in Bangladesh
content: UNICEF’s chief has called for an end to child marriage in Bangladesh. The appeal follows a case in which 14‑year‑old Bushra was at risk of being married off, but community leaders at a UNICEF‑supported child‑protection hub intervened and worked with her father to prevent the forced marriage.
summary: The UNICEF chief called for an end to child marriage in Bangladesh. At age 14, Bushra was prevented from being married off after community leaders at a UNICEF‑supported child protection hub worked with her father.
author: UN News

title: UN cautions against early peacekeeper withdrawal as Sudan war spreads to CAR
content: The United Nations issued a warning on Tuesday, cautioning against an early withdrawal of its peacekeeping forces. The alert comes as the conflict in Sudan expands into the Central African Republic, raising concerns that the region’s security situation may deteriorate if peacekeepers leave prematurely.
summary: The UN warned on Tuesday against a premature withdrawal of its peacekeepers. The warning came as the war in Sudan spilled over into the Central African Republic.
author: UN News

title: UN disarmament chief warns AI is crowding out human judgment in warfare
content: Artificial intelligence is already being widely used on the battlefield, and the role of human judgment in military operations is shrinking rapidly, the head of the UN’s independent disarmament research institute warned on Tuesday.
summary: Artificial intelligence is already being widely used on the battlefield. The head of the UN’s independent disarmament research institute warned on Tuesday that human judgment in military operations is shrinking rapidly.
author: UN News

title: Bloomberg pledges $80M for Democrats as Trump eyes $400M for Republicans
content:
Billionaire former New York City mayor Michael Bloomberg announced he will spend $80 million to support Democratic candidates in the upcoming midterm elections, focusing the money on House races as the party seeks to regain a congressional majority, according to U.S. media reports on Tuesday.

On the same day, former President Donald Trump said he plans to allocate a total of $400 million to assist Republican candidates, noting that $300 million of that amount has already been distributed.
summary: Billionaire former New York City mayor Michael Bloomberg will spend $80 million to help Democratic candidates in the midterm elections. Donald Trump announced he intends to spend $400 million to aid Republican candidates, with $300 million already disbursed.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump claims $400 million spent to back Republicans in midterms
content:
Donald Trump said he will have spent $400 million to support Republican candidates in the upcoming midterm elections.  

The president also announced an incentive program for people to report fraud, noting the administration’s continued focus on Minnesota. In a separate report, the nonpartisan Public Religion Research Institute released its annual American Values Survey, which found that 42 % of white evangelical Protestants do not view empathy as a foundational moral value, while 54 % say empathy can be dangerous when it leads people away from a society guided by God’s truth.
summary: Trump said he will have spent $400 million to support Republican candidates in the upcoming midterm elections. He also announced an incentive program for people to report fraud.
author: Guardian World

title: ‘I’ll make you famous’: court hears recording of Tommy Robinson threat to Daily Mail editor
content: Jurors in a harassment trial heard a voicemail in which far‑right activist Tommy Robinson – whose legal name is Stephen Yaxley‑Lennon – told Daily Mail editor Ted Verity he would make the newspaper’s journalists and their families “famous”. The recording was presented as evidence that Robinson had waged a campaign of harassment against Daily Mail reporters. The trial’s proceedings highlighted the threat to journalists who had written about the activist.
summary: ‘I’ll make you famous’: court hears recording of Tommy Robinson threat to Daily Mail editor.
author: Guardian World

title: Inquest says 5‑month‑old Esta High might have survived meningitis if tested earlier
content:
An inquest jury concluded that five‑month‑old Esta High might have survived had doctors tested her for meningitis earlier, rather than attributing her symptoms to Covid‑19. The baby was admitted to Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023 after presenting with a high temperature and vomiting, and she died a few days later.

The jury’s finding highlights that the delay in testing for meningitis was a factor in the fatal outcome.
summary: Five‑month‑old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023 after being taken to the emergency department with a high temperature and vomiting. An inquest jury concluded she may have been saved had doctors tested her for meningitis sooner instead of attributing her symptoms to Covid‑19.
author: Guardian World

title: Russell Brand told alleged rape victim to “clear up the mess you’ve made,” court hears
content: Woman says alleged assault at comedian’s London home was one of most painful experiences of her life A woman has said she “couldn’t speak or breathe” when Russell Brand raped her at his London townhouse after picking her out from a crowd after one of his gigs, a court has heard. She said the comedian looked “horrified” after the alleged attack so she assumed he would apologise but instead he told her: “Clear up the mess you’ve made.”
summary: A woman testified that Russell Brand raped her at his London townhouse after he picked her from a crowd following one of his gigs. She said she couldn’t speak or breathe, that he looked horrified, and that he told her “Clear up the mess you’ve made.”
author: Guardian World

title: Reform UK policy chief James Orr questioned legality of £72m Harborne, Delo donations
content:
James Orr, then Reform UK’s head of policy and a Cambridge professor, admitted to an undercover reporter that he had concerns about the legality of future donations from billionaire backers Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo under a proposed foreign donors cap.  

These concerns were raised three months before the party received £72 million from Harborne and Delo, and were captured in undercover footage by investigative group Verbatim.
summary: Reform UK policy chief James Orr questioned legality of £72m Harborne, Delo donations.
author: Guardian World

title: Myanmar releases rare photos of detained Aung San Suu Kyi receiving King Charles gift
content:
Myanmar’s military handed two gardening books, a sealed envelope and a sealed diplomatic pouch from Britain’s King Charles to detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi, then released rare photographs of her receiving the items. A presidential spokesperson announced the delivery on social media, noting the king’s known interest in planting and the environment.

Critics described the images as a stunt by the military aimed at reducing Myanmar’s diplomatic isolation. The release of the photos and the gift were therefore framed by observers as a political maneuver rather than a purely humanitarian gesture.
summary: Myanmar’s home ministry handed two gardening books, a sealed envelope and a sealed diplomatic pouch from King Charles to detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi and released rare photos of her receiving the items. Critics said the images were a military stunt aimed at ending the country’s diplomatic isolation.
author: Guardian World

title: 15-year-old harassed after viral video of crude remarks about Modi at Delhi protest
content: ​After a protest clip went viral, a teenager’s life was torn apart by threats that sent her and her family into hiding. Plus, a book on citizen journalism • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Before 24 July, a person I will call R was preoccupied with the ordinary routines of teenage life: experimenting with makeup, grumbling over mathematics homework and hanging out with friends at a tea stall. That month, as the fever of student protests spread across the country, the 15-year-old watched on her phone as young people poured into Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in Delhi, demanding education reform. She went too. But an 11-second video clip from the protest site, in which she made crude and profane remarks about the prime minister, Narendra Modi, upended her life.
summary: A 15‑year‑old teenager posted an 11‑second video from a Jantar Mantar protest in which she made crude and profane remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi. After the clip went viral, she and her family received threats that forced them into hiding and prevented her from leaving home.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump and Zelensky at odds despite Zelensky’s hug with Steve Witkoff in Oslo
content:
Paul Adams notes that a hug between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and real‑estate developer Steve Witkoff in Oslo is unlikely to ease doubts about U.S. policy toward Ukraine.  

The headline adds that President Donald Trump and President Zelensky appear at loggerheads despite the optimism expressed in Oslo.
summary: The Ukrainian leader's hug with Steve Witkoff in the Norwegian capital is unlikely to dispel misgivings about US policy towards his country, writes Paul Adams.
author: BBC World

title: Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Ed Harris star in Other Desert Cities Broadway revival
content:
Jon Robin Baitz’s family reunion drama, Other Desert Cities, has returned to the Hudson Theatre in New York, featuring a star-studded cast for its holiday revival. The production marks the stage debuts of Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Joe Keery, while also welcoming back Broadway veterans Ed Harris, Allison Janney, and Lily Rabe. This updated lineup offers a more prominent ensemble than the play’s 2011 premiere.

The review highlights that the performances, particularly from the newcomers, effectively dispel any concerns about the casting being a Hollywood vanity project. Director John Benjamin Hickey’s staging is noted for being well-attuned to the cast’s abilities, which justifies the play’s quick return to the stage. The production is described as a powerful drama about a family reunion that turns into a political minefield, with the Pulitzer finalist play retaining significant relevance.
summary: The revival of Jon Robin Baitz's drama at the Hudson Theatre marks the stage debuts of Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Joe Keery. Ed Harris, Allison Janney, and Lily Rabe return to Broadway in this production directed by John Benjamin Hickey.
author: Guardian Culture

title: The Cycle review: Forensic scientist autopsies father in supernatural horror
content:
The film The Cycle follows Meg, a forensic scientist portrayed by Deborah Ann Woll. The character is described as possessing a steely composure and strong stomach, remaining unfazed by the decomposing flesh she handles daily. Her professional demeanor and appearance disguise this internal resilience.

The movie is characterized as a gloomy-toned psychodrama that initially focuses on an offbeat family dynamic before revealing its horror genre nature. This shift occurs more than halfway through the narrative, culminating in a detailed transformation sequence. While the special effects are noted as potential material for aficionados, some may find the creature design plasticky. The review suggests that the preceding dramatic elements are not bad, even though the later creature-feature aspects are considered a letdown.
summary: The film features forensic scientist Meg, played by Deborah Ann Woll, who autopsies her father in a story that becomes a horror flick halfway through. Critics note that while the initial family drama is engaging, the later creature effects are considered a letdown.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Sanlé Sory’s new exhibition showcases his first colour photographs of Burkina Faso
content: Sanlé Sory is noted for capturing a million photographs over six decades to document rapid change in Burkina Faso. A new exhibition currently highlights the period when he began embracing colour photography.
summary: Sanlé Sory is said to have taken a million photographs over six decades, documenting rapid change in his home country. A new exhibition looks at the moment he embraced colour.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Christina Applegate says she was misdiagnosed with MS, symptoms worsening
content: Christina Applegate said on Tuesday’s release of her “Messy” podcast that she was wrongly diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. She expressed unhappiness with the new information and noted that her symptoms have only gotten worse.
summary: Christina Applegate said she was wrongly diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. In a Tuesday release of her Messy podcast, she said she was not happy about the new information and that her symptoms have only gotten worse.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Vincent Kompany may miss Bayern's Champions League match against Arsenal due to virus
content:
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany is in doubt to oversee the club’s Champions League match against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night. The manager is currently battling a virus that has affected his legs, causing him significant physical difficulty. Consequently, Kompany was unable to attend the team’s training session on Tuesday and delegated the pre-match press conference to his assistant, Aaron Danks, who is poised to take charge of the dugout if Kompany is unavailable.

Kompany’s condition worsened following Bayern’s 6-1 home victory over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday. He struggled through that match and was subsequently advised to rest. In his absence, the club’s sporting director, Max Eberl, addressed the media after the Leipzig game. German reports indicate that Kompany had to lie down on his sofa at home following the match, as the viral infection aggravated an existing hip problem, leaving him barely able to walk.
summary: Vincent Kompany is uncertain to manage Bayern Munich's upcoming Champions League game against Arsenal as he battles a virus affecting his legs. The manager was advised to rest after struggling with the infection and missed his team's training session on Tuesday.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mark Allen says snooker career may be over after Northern Ireland Open loss
content:
Mark Allen, the former world No 1, stated that his snooker career may be over following a 4-2 first-round defeat to Jordan Brown at the Northern Ireland Open in Belfast. The 40-year-old described himself as being in a “bad place” and said, “I don’t see a future with snooker in it,” while appearing tearful after the loss.

This match marked Allen’s first appearance since his world championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April. During that previous encounter, Allen missed a match-ball black at 16-15 in front and lost the deciding frame to Wu, who ultimately won the title.
summary: Former world No 1 Mark Allen stated his career could be over after losing 4-2 to Jordan Brown in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open. Allen described himself as being in a "bad place" and said he does not see a future in the sport.
author: Guardian Sport

title: British Cycling’s best world championships since 2012 overshadowed by off-track issues
content:
British Cycling secured its most successful world track championships campaign since 2012, topping the medal table in the first qualifying event for the 2028 Olympic Games. The squad won six gold, three silver, and three bronze medals in Shanghai, a performance achieved despite a traumatic buildup that saw star sprinter Matt Richardson withdrawn on the eve of the event following allegations of discriminatory remarks.

This sporting success occurred against a backdrop of internal organizational challenges, including looming redundancies as the governing body restructures. Former cyclists and employees have raised concerns over the return of a toxic culture, while the team’s achievement was overshadowed by ongoing allegations of misconduct.
summary: British Cycling won six gold, three silver, and three bronze medals at the Shanghai World Track Championships, topping the medal table in the first qualifying event for the 2028 Olympic Games. This success occurred despite star sprinter Matt Richardson's withdrawal due to discriminatory remarks allegations and ongoing concerns about redundancies and a toxic culture.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Minhas takes 6/40 as Pakistan beat England in tri-series opener
content:
Pakistan secured a victory over England in the opening match of a one-day international tri-series in Rawalpindi, with England falling 87 runs short in their chase. The result marked a strong start for Pakistan, who capitalized on a contest without the pressure of a Dukes ball and in a format they are more accustomed to.

Arafat Minhas was the standout performer, contributing significantly with both bat and ball in only his fifth ODI. The 21-year-old opened his innings with a half-century from the No. 7 position, helping to stabilize Pakistan’s total alongside newcomer Hasan Nawaz. Their partnership helped convert a score of 81 for four into a final total of 302.

Minhas also delivered impressive bowling figures of six for 40, further cementing his impact on the match. His all-round performance was central to Pakistan’s impressive win, providing a welcome result following their previous English summer campaign.
summary: Pakistan defeated England by 87 runs in their one-day international tri-series opener in Rawalpindi. Arafat Minhas scored 59 runs and took six wickets for 40 runs in his fifth ODI.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Liverpool v Villarreal: Champions League live
content: ⚽ Updates from the 8pm BST kick-off at Anfield ⚽ Football clockwatch | Live scores | Table | Mail Scott Villarreal kick off. They’re kicking towards the Kop in this first half. Both sets of fans give their all to this evening’s pre-match dip into the Rodgers and Hammerstein songbook. Nunca caminarás solo! After which the teams take to the field of play. Liverpool in red, Villarreal in yellow, everyone looking real crisp and clean. A fine atmosphere on a rainy night on Merseyside. The close pals Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez embrace before facing off. We’ll be off in a couple of minutes.
summary: Liverpool and Villarreal kicked off their Champions League match at Anfield on a rainy night. The teams took to the field with Liverpool wearing red and Villarreal wearing yellow.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Webb backs VAR over Botman challenge on Jackson
content: Premier League referees' chief Howard Webb says Sven Botman's challenge on Nicolas Jackson was a "high-end reckless challenge" but backed the video assistant referee's decision not to intervene for a red card.
summary: Premier League referees' chief Howard Webb described Sven Botman's challenge on Nicolas Jackson as a high-end reckless challenge. He supported the video assistant referee's decision not to intervene for a red card.
author: BBC Sport

title: Mark Allen considers snooker retirement after Northern Ireland Open exit
content: Mark Allen has stated that retiring from snooker is a decision he has been contemplating for some time. This comment follows his 4-2 defeat by Jordan Brown at the Northern Ireland Open.
summary: Mark Allen stated that retiring from snooker is something he has been contemplating for a while. This comment followed his 4-2 loss to Jordan Brown at the Northern Ireland Open.
author: BBC Sport

title: Cook Political Report shifts Minnesota Senate race toward Democrats
content: The Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan election handicapper, updated its Senate race ratings on Tuesday. The organization moved Minnesota’s Senate race from likely to lean Democrat and shifted South Carolina’s seat from likely Republican to lean Republican. These changes offer both parties grounds for optimism as the midterm elections approach.
summary: The Cook Political Report moved Minnesota's Senate race from likely to lean Democrat and South Carolina's from likely to lean Republican. These changes provide both parties with optimism heading into the midterm elections.
author: The Hill

title: Trump launches $25 million whistleblower program; Nick Shirley receives first payout
content: President Trump and Vice President Vance announced a $25 million Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program designed to reward individuals who report fraud to the federal government. The initiative offers a 1 percent commission for tips that result in successful convictions. Nick Shirley has received the first payout under this new program.
summary: President Trump and Vice President Vance announced a $25 million Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program that pays a 1 percent commission for tips leading to successful convictions. Nick Shirley received the first payout under this new initiative.
author: The Hill

title: Mayor Mamdani says El‑Sayed win critical for NYC
content:
On Tuesday, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) publicly endorsed Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed, saying that a victory for El‑Sayed would signal openness to a new political future in the country.  

The remarks were made during a press conference when a reporter asked Mamdani about whether he would back the candidate, though the question was not fully answered in the available record.
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) expressed support for Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed. He said El‑Sayed's victory would signal openness to a new political future in the country.
author: The Hill

title: Former NATO commander Wesley Clark says Trump’s Russia diesel deal lacks balance
content: Former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Wesley Clark said on Monday there was “no balance” in President Trump’s decision “to give in to Russia” after the administration waived sanctions and allowed Russian diesel imports into the United States, while still supporting Ukraine’s war against the Kremlin. Clark added that the most important thing is to maintain the rights of nations to be free.
summary: Former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Wesley Clark on Monday said there was “no balance” in President Trump’s decision “to give in to Russia” after waiving sanctions and agreeing to permit Russian diesel into the U. S.
author: The Hill

title: Jackdaw North Sea gasfield approved in blow to climate campaigners
content:
The Jackdaw North Sea gasfield is set to receive approval on Wednesday, a decision that signals Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh’s commitment to the North Sea fossil fuel industry. Chancellor John Healey will join Fahnbulleh in Aberdeen to make the announcement following more than a year of deliberations regarding whether the project would violate UK climate commitments.

The move is expected to trigger disputes with climate campaigners and Labour MPs, potentially undermining the party’s green credentials.
summary: The Jackdaw gasfield will receive approval on Wednesday, signaling Andy Burnham's commitment to the North Sea fossil fuel industry. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh and Chancellor John Healey will make the announcement from Aberdeen after more than a year of deliberations.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Great white shark photobombs California beachgoers at Marina State Beach
content: A great white shark leaped several feet from the water off Marina state beach over the weekend, photobombing a group of friends posing for photos. Videos circulating online capture the shark launching itself into the air in the background while the visitors take pictures along the California shoreline.
summary: A great white shark leaped several feet from the water off Marina State Beach over the weekend. Videos show the shark appearing in the background as a group of friends posed for photos.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Medical students learn from conversations with care home residents
content: First-year medical students visit care homes to engage in conversation with older residents. This task, which lacks a specific medical history or diagnostic goal, can initially feel daunting for students as they focus on getting to know the individuals.
summary: First-year medical students visited care homes to engage in conversations with older residents. The task focused on getting to know the residents rather than taking medical histories or making diagnoses.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds AI chatbots detect redundant medical tests but struggle with medical disagreements
content:
A new joint study by Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (BGU) and Clalit Health Services indicates that leading large language models (LLMs) effectively identify redundant medical interventions in most scenarios. The research addresses the growing reliance on artificial intelligence for medical advice, specifically examining whether AI can determine when tests or treatments are unnecessary.

The findings show that these AI systems stumble primarily in gray areas where medical consensus is divided. By highlighting this specific limitation, the study provides insight into the capabilities and boundaries of current AI tools in clinical decision-making contexts.
summary: A joint study by Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and Clalit Health Services shows that leading large language models successfully identify when medical interventions are redundant. These AI systems primarily stumble in gray areas where medical consensus is divided.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New Medicaid rules require 80 monthly work or education hours starting 2027
content: Beginning in January 2027, millions of low-income adults with Medicaid coverage will be required to document at least 80 hours of employment, job training, volunteering, or education each month to maintain their insurance coverage.
summary: Beginning in January 2027, millions of low-income adults with Medicaid must document at least 80 hours of employment, job training, volunteering, or education each month. This requirement is necessary to maintain their insurance coverage.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Parents of transgender youth face mental health declines after 2025 US presidential inauguration
content: In early 2025, a series of executive orders issued by the US president directly threatened and restricted the rights of transgender youth. This shift in policy occurred against a backdrop where transgender youth already experienced higher levels of mental health distress than their peers. The provided text raises questions regarding whether these events further worsened the mental health of transgender youth and how they impacted their parents.
summary: The 2025 US presidential inauguration marked a shift in reality for transgender youth following executive orders that restricted their rights. This article examines whether these events worsened the mental health of transgender youth and how they affected their parents.
author: Medical Xpress

title: St. Jude-led study finds combination therapy slows aggressive osteosarcoma growth
content:
Scientists co-led by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital identified a potential therapeutic vulnerability in certain forms of osteosarcoma, as described in the Journal of Experimental Medicine. In preclinical models of this pediatric bone cancer, a combination approach slowed tumor growth and prolonged survival.

The therapy degraded EP300, a protein co-opted to express oncogenes in many cancers, while simultaneously inhibiting AKT, a well-known cancer drug target. These findings highlight the clinical potential of the combination strategy.
summary: Scientists co-led by St. Jude Children's Research Hospital identified a therapeutic vulnerability in osteosarcoma by combining therapies that degrade EP300 and inhibit AKT. This approach slowed tumor growth and prolonged survival in preclinical models of the pediatric bone cancer.

title: NASA tests roamx-0201 blade design to boost Mars helicopter range to 18.7 km
content: Ingenuity roamx-0201 Ingenuity roamx-0201 Ingenuity roamx-0201 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Image Details Rotor blade cross-sections highlight the thinner profile of the roamx-0201 design (right) compared to the more traditional, rounded shape used by NASA’s Ingenuity Mars helicopter, which accomplished the first powered flight on Mars. NASA researchers are developing the future of flight on Mars, laying the groundwork for helicopters with the ability to fly higher and farther while conducting science on the Red Planet. Using high-fidelity computer simulations and wind tunnel tests, engineers are reimagining the rotorcraft blades that could carry the next generation of Mars flyers. NASA’s Ingenuity helicopter made history as the first powered aircraft to fly on another planet. The SkyFall mission, scheduled for launch in 2028, builds on that legacy with a trio of helicopters destined for Mars exploration. Both missions utilize a blade designed to operate in Mars’ thin atmosphere, with a curved edge reminiscent of but distinct from blades used on Earth. Researchers are exploring unconventional blade designs that are thinner and sharper, aiming to enable future missions after Skyfall to expand their single-flight range across Mars. One team at NASA’s Ames Research Center in California’s Silicon Valley is working with Imperial College London, United Kingdom, and Nagoya University, Japan, to test a new blade cross-section, or airfoil, that promises to significantly boost aerodynamic performance on Mars. Researchers designed the new airfoil, called roamx-0201, using advanced simulations and algorithms tuned to Mars conditions, pointing researchers toward a thinner, asymmetrical shape. Subsequent wind tunnel tests showed that the optimized design boosted performance and was better able to recover in risky flight conditions. Researchers used high-fidelity simulation tools to analyze the performance of the roamx-0201 airfoil and compare it to Ingenuity’s capacity. They found that the redesigned blades could enable future Mars helicopters to expand the distances that can be covered in one uninterrupted flight from Ingenuity’s 0.7 kilometers to as much as 18.7 kilometers while carrying scientific instruments. The findings were announced in a paper published Sept. 22 in the journal of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics. The roamx‑0201 blades performed well in part because they were able to operate longer at higher speeds before experiencing a phenomenon known as “drag divergence”, where performance drops suddenly when the rotors approach the speed of sound, which is lower on Mars than on Earth. The new blade also differs from earlier designs in how it uses turbulence to create lift. As air flows over a rotorcraft blade, it forms a thin region called the “boundary layer.” The new airfoil intentionally disrupts the flow of that boundary layer at the front of the airfoil directly at the leading edge to create a disturbance that, counterintuitively, pulls the blade upward to help lift the rotorcraft more effectively than with earlier designs. Another challenge for rotorcraft is “stall,” an aerodynamic condition in which performance drops sharply and flight becomes unstable following a change in the angle of airflow. Ingenuity’s blades experienced steep performance degradation at stall, but under the conditions studied, the roamx-0201 design showed significantly improved stall behavior. That means future helicopters could operate safely at a wider range of flight angles. While the technology is not yet ready for Mars, tests are helping engineers understand and resolve discrepancies between computational predictions and real-world performance. Ongoing research across NASA aims to enable more efficient Mars helicopters that can fly farther, carry more payload, and unlock new science and discovery missions.
summary: NASA tests roamx-0201 blade design to boost Mars helicopter range to 18.7 km.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Advances SR-1 Freedom Nuclear Power Module for 2028 Mars Mission
content:
NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom mission, announced during the agency’s “Ignition” event, is designed to become the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth’s orbit. The mission aims to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space while delivering the SkyFall science payload to Mars. The spacecraft’s nuclear power module, situated at the end of a boom, consists of a reactor that generates heat through nuclear fission and a power conversion system that transforms that heat into electricity for onboard systems and propulsion.

To advance development, NASA and its partners have agreed to key contract actions intended to reduce technical risk and maintain momentum toward a late 2028 launch. Steve Sinacore, the SR-1 Freedom program director, stated that these actions strengthen collaboration and ensure the mission is on track to build a foundation for NASA’s first fission-powered voyage beyond Earth orbit. The agreements also aim to develop technology that is extensible to future space nuclear applications.

Sierra Lobo Inc. will provide the closed Brayton cycle power conversion system, which converts thermal energy from the fission reactor into electrical power. This work is being conducted under the Space Flight Systems Development and Operations Contract III, awarded in 2024, to support hardware design, development, testing, and operations at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland. The power conversion system will be integrated with the fission reactor, which is being designed and developed by the Department of Energy’s Idaho National Laboratory.

Safety protocols for the SR-1 Freedom spacecraft include interagency safety reviews, continuous oversight by a NASA chief safety officer, and a rigorous design process focusing on hazards, failure tolerance, and nuclear safety. The nuclear reactor portion of the spacecraft will remain inactive until it leaves Earth orbit. Upon arrival at Mars, the mission will deploy the SkyFall science mission, a team of three Mars helicopters evolved from the Ingenuity design, to collect scientific data, demonstrate exploration zones, and identify potential water sources.
summary: NASA and partners have agreed to key contract actions to advance the development of the Space Reactor-1 Freedom nuclear power module, targeting a 2028 launch. Sierra Lobo Inc. will provide the power conversion system, which will be integrated with a reactor designed by the Department of Energy's Idaho National Laboratory.
author: NASA News

title: French Government Orders Platforms to Remove Protest Footage and Looted Goods
content: The French government has convened emergency meetings with digital platforms to address ongoing protests. TikTok and other sites were instructed to limit the spread of protest footage and AI-altered images. Additionally, online retailers such as Vinted and eBay reportedly signed an agreement to prevent looted goods from appearing on resale sites.
summary: The French government held emergency meetings with TikTok and other sites, instructing them to curb protest footage and AI-altered images. Online retailers like Vinted and eBay reportedly agreed to stop looted goods from appearing on resale sites.
author: Wired

title: Tuesday Labs opens reservations for $20,000 Voxel home robot
content:
Tuesday Labs, a New York City–based robotics lab and design studio, has opened reservations for its new bi‑pedal robot, Voxel. The company describes Voxel as a “droid butler” that can learn and take over routine tasks around the home. The robot features a pair of highly‑articulated arms and an advanced vision system, positioning it alongside other household‑robot makers such as Weave Robotics’ Issac 1.

Customers can reserve a Voxel for $200, with the full price expected to be about $20,000 when the robot ships in 2028. The model available for preorder is known, though further details are not yet disclosed.
summary: Tuesday Labs, a New York City robotics lab and design studio, has opened reservations for Voxel, a bi‑pedal robot that can learn and perform routine household tasks. The preorder costs $200, with full pricing expected around $20,000 when the robot ships in 2028.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft reportedly plans Xbox handheld in 2027, next-gen console in 2028
content:
According to a report from Fortune, Microsoft plans to release an Xbox next-generation handheld device during the holiday season of 2027. This is followed by the launch of the next-generation console, codenamed Project Helix, in the holidays of 2028. The report does not specify whether the handheld will be manufactured by a partner like Asus or by Microsoft directly, though the company previously collaborated with Asus for its Xbox Ally devices.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has described Project Helix as a "family of devices," indicating that the next-generation console may consist of multiple components rather than a single unit.
summary: Microsoft is reportedly planning to launch an Xbox "next-generation handheld device" for the holiday season of 2027. The Xbox next-gen console, codename Project Helix, would then launch in the holidays of 2028, according to a new report from Fortune.
author: The Verge

title: JustWatch launches ad-supported streaming service with 30 global partners
content:
JustWatch has launched JustWatch TV, a new streaming service that follows its announcement of plans to enter the market last month. The platform offers an ad-supported free subscription, an ad-free paid tier, and movie rentals. Content is sourced from 30 global partners, including Bleecker Street, Cineverse, and Fremantle.

The service is accessible via JustWatch’s existing mobile apps and website. It is currently available in 12 markets, which include the US, Canada, France, Italy, Australia, and the UK.
summary: JustWatch TV offers an ad-supported free subscription, an ad-free paid plan, and movie rentals from 30 global partners. The service is currently available in 12 markets, including the US, Canada, and the UK, through existing mobile apps and the website.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon Fire HD 10 drops to $72.99 as company phases out budget tablets
content:
Amazon is phasing out its Fire HD tablets in favor of higher-priced Alexa Tablets, a move that signals the end of an era for affordable options from the retailer. Despite this transition, the ad-supported Amazon Fire HD 10 (2023) remains available at a discounted price of $72.99, representing an $82 reduction from its original $139.99 cost. This 32GB model is currently priced slightly lower than the Fire HD 8, making it a budget-friendly choice for users seeking basic multimedia and web browsing capabilities.

The device features a 10.1-inch 1080p display, which offers a sharper and larger viewing experience compared to the lower-resolution screen of the Fire HD 8. It includes better front-facing cameras for video calls and provides up to 13 hours of battery life, suitable for long travel periods. For users requiring more space, a microSD card slot allows storage expansion up to 1TB for offline apps, movies, and books. The tablet also retains a 3.5mm headphone jack, a feature absent in newer iPads.

Software-wise, the Fire HD 10 runs Amazon’s Fire OS rather than Android, though it supports the Alexa Plus AI assistant for Prime members. While the system allows for the sideloading of Android apps, the device's low-end specifications may result in poor performance for more demanding applications and games. Amazon has stated that the tablet will continue to receive security updates, ensuring ongoing support for users who purchase it during this promotional period.
summary: The Fire HD 10 offers a sharper, larger screen than its smaller siblings. | Image: Amazon Amazon recently announced it’s phasing out its Fire HD tablets in favor of much pricier Alexa Tablets.
author: The Verge

title: Xbox CEO is reportedly planning three more rounds of layoffs
content:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is reportedly planning three additional rounds of layoffs in November and January, according to Fortune. These moves follow a July announcement of an organizational "reset" that included 3,200 planned job cuts over Microsoft’s 2027 fiscal year, with 1,600 reductions occurring immediately. In September, Microsoft also laid off approximately 260 employees.

Sharma’s broader strategic changes have involved allowing Double Fine and Compulsion Games to become independent studios again, while the developer of Senua, Ninja Theory, may close. The report also notes speculation regarding a potential spin-off or sale of Xbox, referencing comments from Judson Althoff, the CEO of Microsoft’s commercial division.
summary: Xbox CEO is reportedly planning three more rounds of layoffs.
author: The Verge

title: DJI Osmo Pocket 3 vlogging camera discounted to $395
content:
DJI’s Osmo Pocket 3 vlogging camera is currently available for $395 at retailers including Amazon, Best Buy, and B&H Photo, representing a discount from its standard price of $499. The device is described as a significant upgrade from smartphone video capabilities, featuring a large 1-inch CMOS sensor mounted to a built-in gimbal for smooth, stable movement. This configuration allows users to capture high-quality footage of travels, activities, or daily routines without the need for extensive exposure adjustments or heavy post-processing.

The compact camera includes a 2-inch rotatable screen for framing shots and reviewing footage on the go, along with three built-in microphones. While the internal mics are sufficient for many uses, the camera also supports connection to DJI’s Mic Mini wireless mics. The Osmo Pocket 3 is capable of shooting video at up to 4K resolution at 120 frames per second. Its small size makes it easy to store in a pocket or small bag, and its video results are often compared to those of more expensive dedicated mirrorless digital cameras.

Although a DJI Osmo Pocket 4 exists, it is not officially for sale in the United States. The current deal on the Pocket 3 is presented as an option for individuals seeking a dedicated vlogging camera that offers professional-grade stabilization and image quality in a portable form factor.
summary: The DJI Osmo Pocket 3 is available for $395 at retailers including Amazon, Best Buy, and B&H Photo, down from its usual $499 price. The camera features a 1-inch sensor, a built-in gimbal, and 4K video capabilities.
author: The Verge

title: Polestar partners with Oxford to measure driver response to performance
content:
Polestar is collaborating with researchers at the University of Oxford to investigate the impact of car performance on drivers. While traditional automotive metrics such as acceleration, top speed, and lap times are easily measured using standard tools like stopwatches and tracks, the subjective experience of driving a high-performance vehicle remains difficult to quantify. The company aims to address this gap by exploring how performance affects the driver, moving beyond the current industry focus on zero-to-60 mph times in the electric vehicle sector.

The initiative highlights a shift from purely mechanical measurements to human-centric analysis. Although the source notes that the desire for speed has historical roots, from horseback riding to modern motorized vehicles, it emphasizes that measuring the driver’s response to that speed is a distinct challenge. By partnering with academic experts, Polestar seeks to develop methods for assessing the human element of driving performance, a question that standard automotive testing does not typically answer.
summary: Polestar is collaborating with researchers at the University of Oxford to quantify the effect of car performance on the driver. This research aims to measure the driver's experience, which is distinct from standard metrics like acceleration and top speed.
author: Ars Technica

title: JustWatch launches free ad-supported streaming service
content: JustWatch, a streaming search guide used by 50 million people, is launching its own streaming service. The new platform will offer free, ad-supported movies and shows, along with a $3.99-per-month ad-free tier and movie rentals.
summary: The streaming search guide JustWatch is launching its own streaming service. It will offer free ad-supported content, a $3.99 monthly ad-free tier, and movie rentals.

title: Meta’s Muse Surpasses 10M U.S. Downloads in 40 Days, Joining Elite Apps
content:
Meta's AI companion Muse has surpassed 10 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days, joining an exclusive group of apps that includes Threads.  

New data also shows Muse is retaining users at higher rates than its AI rivals.
summary: Meta's AI companion Muse has surpassed 10 million U. S.

title: ChatGPT Adds Lock Feature to Keep Chats Private During Device Sharing
content:
ChatGPT has added a new “lock” feature that lets users secure individual chats.  

According to the company, the lock is intended for situations where a user is discussing something personal or planning a surprise. It allows the conversation to remain private even if the device is handed to a friend or family member to view a different chat.
summary: ChatGPT has introduced a lock feature that allows users to keep chats private. The feature is intended for personal discussions or surprise planning when users hand their device to friends or family to show them something in another chat.

title: New Chinese Brands Draw Curiosity at Paris Mondial de l'Auto
content:
Half a million visitors flocked to Paris for the Mondial de l'Auto, making it one of the most attended automotive events of the year.

The presence of new Chinese brands at the show attracted large crowds of curious European car fans, highlighting growing interest in these emerging manufacturers.
summary: Half a million visitors flocked to Paris for the Mondial de l'Auto. The presence of new Chinese brands drew large crowds of curious European car fans.

title: Australian police charge man after lawmaker Helen Haines hit by car
content:
Australia police say a man has been charged after lawmaker Helen Haines was deliberately hit by a car.  

Haines was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her office in Wangaratta, a town just over 200 kilometres northeast of Melbourne, at approximately 0635 CET on Monday.
summary: Australian police have charged a man in connection with the deliberate car attack on lawmaker Helen Haines. Haines was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her office in Wangaratta at about 0635 CET on Monday.

title: Paris shop owners clean up and repair stores after riots
content: Shop owners and cleanup crews cleared debris and repaired vandalized storefronts in Paris on Monday. The restoration efforts followed two nights of rioting and looting that damaged shops across the city.
summary: Shop owners and cleanup crews cleared debris and repaired vandalised storefronts in Paris on Monday. The damage was caused by two nights of rioting and looting that left shops across the city damaged.

title: IRGC threatens to target undersea cables after warning Washington of retaliation
content: Iran’s foreign ministry has warned Washington that it would retaliate against any strike, reinforcing Tehran’s stance on potential military responses. An IRGC spokesperson has further escalated tensions by threatening to target undersea internet cables in the Gulf, adding a new dimension to the ongoing war of words between Tehran and Washington.
summary: Iran’s foreign ministry warned Washington it would retaliate against any strike. An IRGC spokesperson threatened to target undersea internet cables in the Gulf.
author: Euronews

title: Macron Begins State Visit to Qatar as Part of Wider Gulf Tour
content:
France's President Emmanuel Macron began a state visit to Qatar, arriving in Doha where he was received with full state honours. The visit is part of a broader Gulf tour aimed at strengthening strategic ties between France and Qatar.

Macron is seeking energy deals with Gulf partners to ease fuel prices in France amid domestic protests, while also contributing to regional stability.
summary: Qatar welcomed French President Macron with full state honours upon his arrival in Doha. Macron is seeking energy deals with Gulf partners to ease fuel prices in France amid domestic protests, while also contributing to regional stability.
author: Euronews

title: Guardia Civil rescues family and dogs from flooded home in Oliva, Spain
content:
Spanish Guardia Civil officers rescued a family and their dogs from a flooded home in Oliva, eastern Spain.  

Footage shows officers carrying residents to safety as floodwaters engulf the town, while aerial images reveal the extent of flooding across the Valencia region.
summary: Spanish Guardia Civil officers rescued a family and their dogs from a flooded home in Oliva, eastern Spain. Footage shows officers carrying residents to safety as floodwaters engulf the town and aerial images reveal the extent of the flooding across the Valencia region.
author: Euronews

title: Alberta rejects independence referendum, 76% vote to stay in Canada
content: Alberta rejected a plan to hold a binding independence referendum, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta. With more than 1.5 million votes counted, 76 % supported remaining in Canada while about 24 % favored beginning a process toward separation. The outcome is a win for unity amid worsening ties with the United States.
summary: Alberta rejected a plan to hold a binding independence referendum, with results announced Tuesday. Unofficial results from Elections Alberta, based on more than 1.5 million votes, showed about 76% supported remaining in Canada and close to 24% backed beginning a separation process.
author: France 24

title: France's decades-long ties with Gulf states built on 'economic development, oil, defence agreements'
content:
François Gouyette, former French ambassador to the UAE and Saudi Arabia, discussed France’s Gulf diplomacy on a podcast hosted by Genie Godula. He noted that President Emmanuel Macron’s recent visit serves a dual purpose: alleviating France’s energy pressures and reaffirming longstanding defense partnerships with Gulf monarchies. Gouyette emphasized that France must play its role as a key partner, framing the engagement within the context of domestic economic security and international strategic commitments.

Gouyette characterized French military assistance as an expression of strategic solidarity rather than direct participation in the conflict with Iran. This diplomatic approach highlights the decades-long ties between France and Gulf states, which are built on economic development, oil, and defense agreements. The discussion addressed how these relationships navigate the blurred boundaries between national economic needs and regional security obligations amidst escalating Middle East tensions.
summary: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome François Gouyette, former French ambassador to the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Against a backdrop of violent unrest at home and escalating conflict in the Middle East, French President Emmanuel Macron's Gulf diplomacy underscores the increasingly blurred boundaries between domestic economic security and international strategic commitments.
author: France 24

title: France Maintains Curfews in Cities After Violent October 17 Protests
content:
French cities that imposed a curfew on Monday experienced a generally calm night after protests on Oct. 17 devolved into violent riots over the weekend.  

Despite criticism from citizens, the French government said it would maintain the curfew where necessary on Tuesday night.
summary: French cities that imposed a curfew Monday saw a generally calm night after violent riots during the October 17 protests. Despite criticism from citizens, France's government said it is maintaining the measure where necessary on Tuesday night.
author: France 24

title: Sudan Drone Strike on Abyei Market Kills 153, Fuel Depot Fire Rages
content:
A drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region killed at least 153 people. The attack also left dozens injured, and a fire at a nearby fuel depot continued to burn into Tuesday.  

Local officials have blamed Sudan’s military for Monday’s strike.
summary: At least 153 people were killed in a drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region. Local officials blamed Sudan’s military for the attack, which also left dozens injured and a nearby fuel depot fire continued to burn.
author: France 24

title: French police use social media to identify looters from last weekend's unrest
content: French police are using social media to identify and arrest suspects linked to last weekend’s looting and unrest. Investigators are scrutinising online videos together with footage from thousands of security cameras to track suspects and gather evidence. The crackdown follows the government’s vow to hold those responsible for the violence and shop damage accountable.
summary: French police are using social media to identify and arrest suspects linked to last weekend’s looting and unrest. Investigators are scrutinising online videos together with footage from thousands of security cameras to track suspects and gather evidence, as the government vows to hold those responsible accountable.
author: France 24

title: Paris police impose new curfew in central districts from 2100 GMT Tuesday
content:
Paris police have imposed a new curfew on parts of the city for Tuesday night. The order, issued after a previous curfew that authorities said restored calm following weekend riots and looting, will run from 2100 GMT Tuesday to 0400 GMT Wednesday.

The curfew covers the République public square in the city’s central east—an area where many clashes occurred over the weekend—and the central Les Halles district, known for its shops. The announcement was reported by FRANCE 24’s Luke Shrago from central Paris.
summary: Paris police ordered a new curfew for parts of the city on Tuesday night after a previous curfew restored calm following weekend riots and looting. The curfew runs from 2100 GMT Tuesday to 0400 GMT Wednesday and applies to the Republique public square in central east Paris and the central les Halles district.
author: France 24

title: Hundreds face immediate trials for ransacking French city centres
content: Hundreds of people are now on immediate trial for ransacking city centres across France, according to France 24’s Delano D’Souza. Since 17 October, more than 2,000 individuals have been taken into police custody, with nearly 70 % of them adults. The ongoing trials are examining the defendants’ profiles, alleged actions, the evidence and the penalties they may face.
summary: Since the 17th of October, over 2,000 people have been placed in police custody in France, with nearly 70% adults. Trials have begun to examine their profiles, actions, evidence and likely penalties.
author: France 24

title: Zelensky meets US envoy Steve Witkoff to try to rescue strained relations
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was meeting US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Tuesday in a ​bid to rescue relations that have sunk to new lows as President Donald Trump has courted Moscow and Kyiv has complained about Washington withholding vital defences. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kharkiv.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Tuesday in a bid to rescue relations that have sunk to new lows. The meeting comes as President Donald Trump has courted Moscow and Kyiv has complained about Washington withholding vital defences, reported from Kharkiv by FRANCE 24’s Gulliver Cragg.
author: France 24

title: Women lead India's youth‑led “Cockroach” protests despite harassment and arrests
content: Women are marching in large numbers across Indian cities as part of the youth‑led “Cockroach” protests, despite facing online harassment and police detentions. In the context of a broad crackdown, they are rejecting the label of victims and taking to the streets.
summary: Women are taking to the streets of Indian cities in large numbers for the youth‑led “Cockroach” protests, facing online harassment and police detentions. They refuse to be seen as victims amid a large‑scale crackdown.
author: DW World

title: Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro virtually tied in polls before Brazil runoff
content: Polls released less than a week before Brazil’s decisive presidential runoff indicate that incumbent left‑wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right‑wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro are virtually tied in the race. The close numbers suggest a highly competitive contest heading into the vote.
summary: Polls show left‑wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right‑wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro are virtually tied. The decisive presidential runoff election is less than a week away.
author: DW World

title: Sudan drone strike kills dozens in Abyei market, sparks fuel depot fire
content: A drone strike hit a market in the disputed Abyei border region, igniting a fuel depot and causing a large fire. The attack killed around 150 people, with officials describing the death toll as dozens. South Sudanese officials attributed the strike to Sudan’s military.
summary: A drone strike hit a market in the Abyei border region disputed by Sudan and South Sudan, killing dozens. The strike ignited a fuel depot, causing a large fire, and South Sudanese officials blamed Sudan's military.
author: DW World

title: UNIFIL mandate ends as Lebanon faces uncertainty, EU mission to aid army
content: UN peacekeeping forces are preparing to withdraw from Lebanon, leaving Israel still present in the country and Hezbollah remaining armed. A new EU support mission has been announced to strengthen the Lebanese army, but it will not replace the departing UN peacekeepers.
summary: UN peacekeeping forces are preparing to withdraw from Lebanon as the UNIFIL mandate nears its end. An EU support mission will aim to strengthen Lebanon's army but will not replace the departing UN peacekeepers, while Israel remains present and Hezbollah stays armed.
author: DW World

title: French police use force to repress dissent, drawing criticism for violent tactics
content:
French police are described as instruments of the state whose primary role is to repress public dissent rather than manage it. The article cites familiar images of tear‑gas clouds over Paris squares, baton charges against masked protesters and teenagers, and the use of stun grenades, noting that these scenes have recently drawn global attention to France’s policing methods.

In contrast, the piece observes that most Western European neighbours tend to favour crowd‑containment and de‑escalation tactics, whereas France has historically responded to street‑based social movements with what it characterises as “shocking physical force.”
summary: French police are described as instruments of the state whose job is to repress public dissent. Their tactics have included teargas, baton charges and stun grenades, contrasting with neighboring countries that favor crowd containment and de‑escalation.
author: Guardian World

title: Republicans threaten to withhold support over Trump's softening stance on Ukraine
content: GOP lawmakers threaten to pull support for president’s agenda after Russia diesel deal and sanctions pause US politics live – latest updates A handful of Republicans have spoken out against Donald Trump ’s softening stance on Russia, threatening to pull financial support for his agenda over his “embarrassing” handling of the Ukraine war. Don Bacon, an outgoing congressman in Nebraska, condemned Trump’s actions – which include a stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel and the pausing of sanctions on Moscow – as “absolutely disgraceful” and accused the US president of cozying up to a “war criminal” in Vladimir Putin, his Russian counterpart.
summary: Republicans threaten to withhold support over Trump's softening stance on Ukraine.
author: Guardian World

title: Nato adds assets to Black Sea as Russia attacks five merchant vessels
content: NATO is deploying additional military assets to the Black Sea as Russia’s war on Ukraine extends to the alliance’s borders, targeting vessels that carry agricultural cargo. The move follows a recent spike in deadly Russian attacks on merchant shipping, with five vessels hit on Tuesday. Russia’s military reported striking three cargo ships in Ukraine’s port of Reni and two other cargo vessels while they were en route to Odesa. The escalation has heightened anxiety over the security of maritime trade in the region.
summary: Nato is deploying additional military assets to the Black Sea amid a recent deadly escalation of Russian attacks on merchant shipping. Russia’s military said it struck three cargo vessels in Ukraine’s port of Reni and two other cargo vessels en route to Odesa on Tuesday.
author: Guardian World

title: US resumes sharing missile strike intelligence with Ukraine, says Zelenskyy
content:
Zelenskyy said the United States has resumed sharing intelligence with Kyiv about Russian missile strikes after a meeting with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff in Norway.

He added that Ukraine is again receiving advance warnings of ballistic missile attacks, which had seemed suspended last week by the White House.

Zelenskyy said, “Now it works. It’s great,” and that the U.S. move would save lives.
summary: US resumes sharing missile strike intelligence with Ukraine, says Zelenskyy.
author: Guardian World

title: Alleged attacker Brendan Nugent to appear in Wangaratta court for Helen Haines case
content: Follow the day’s news live. Deeply appalled’: politicians condemn alleged attack after Helen Haines critically injured Helen Haines, the principled MP respected across parliament Helen Haines’ alleged attacker, Brendan Nugent, has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally cause serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official. He was held overnight to appear at Wangaratta magistrates court this morning at 9.30am, Victoria police confirmed in a statement, adding that it would be alleged the attack was targeted.
summary: Follow the day’s news live. content:
Far‑right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro appeared in a primetime television debate opposite left‑wing opponent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva with the word “corrupto” (corrupt) written on the palm of his hand. The gesture was intended to highlight his rival’s alleged crookedness on the eve of Brazil’s presidential election runoff.

Social media users quickly turned the stunt into a viral meme, parodying the display and indicating that the tactic backfired. The incident has generated widespread online commentary ahead of the runoff.

content: Mitchell Fairbarn, a Canadian tourist, was found guilty of animal cruelty on Monday after prosecutors said he snatched a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at an iconic Las Vegas hotel. The court heard that the 27‑year‑old bird was hurt and frightened during the incident. Prosecutors characterized the act as a malicious prank, while Fairbarn’s lawyer described it as drunken foolishness that was not intended to harm the bird.

content:
Police in Guinea‑Bissau raided the offices of a group of vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services secretary. Judicial police seized doses of hepatitis B vaccine from the researchers, officials said in a Facebook post.

The researchers are at the center of a dispute over studies involving African newborns. Their work has been funded with $1.6 million from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a combined $3.2 million.

title: The view from the edge of a sparkling spiral galaxy | Space photo of the day for Oct. 20, 2026
content:
The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a striking side-on view of the spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located approximately 37 million light-years from Earth. The image, taken by the telescope’s Advanced Camera for Surveys, reveals the galaxy’s edge as a sparkling band of stars and brown ribbons of dust. Although the distinct spiral arms are not clearly visible from this perspective, the galaxy is classified as an "intermediate" spiral, meaning its structure falls between that of barred and unbarred spiral galaxies.

The photograph highlights a particularly luminous blue star featuring four diffraction spikes, an effect created by light bending through Hubble’s camera components. This observation is part of a broader Hubble survey aimed at studying 260 satellite galaxies that are gravitationally bound to larger host systems. The survey specifically targets satellites near host galaxies similar to the Milky Way, with 111 such satellites identified so far.

Researchers are using these observations to investigate the complex dynamics within low-mass galaxies like NGC 1827 and their interactions with their host systems. The image was processed by Gladys Kober at NASA/Catholic University of America, with original credit to NASA, ESA, and Michael Jones at the California Institute of Technology.
summary: The spiral galaxy NGC 1827, as seen from the side by the Hubble Space Telescope. (Image credit: NASA, ESA, Michael Jones (California Institute of Technology); Image Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America)) If you were approaching the edge of a spiral galaxy, arriving from afar through the cosmos, it might look something like this.

title: Stargazing apps: How to use red light filters to preserve night vision
content:
Stargazing applications can enhance the observation of the night sky by using augmented reality to identify stars or providing details on events like lunar eclipses. However, the bright light emitted by smartphone screens can interfere with a user’s ability to see distant objects. This issue is particularly relevant for those using telescopes, as bright screens prevent the eyes from adjusting to the dark environment.

When in the dark, it can take up to 20 to 30 minutes for vision to fully adjust. During this period, rod cells in the eyes build up a chemical called rhodopsin, which enables night vision. Exposure to bright light bleaches this chemical, negatively impacting the ability to see fainter celestial objects such as galaxies and nebulas. While putting a phone away to allow for adjustment is one solution, it is not feasible for users who rely on stargazing apps for navigation.

Many stargazing apps include features to minimize white light, such as a red light filter, though this option may be restricted in free versions. In SkyView, users can enable this by tapping the screen, selecting the horizontal lines, navigating to Settings and then Display, and choosing Night Mode and Red. For Star Walk 2, the process involves tapping the horizontal lines, going to Settings, and tapping the button next to Night Mode. In Sky Tonight, users tap the horizontal lines, select Settings, then Tools, and finally Night Mode. These settings reduce white light within the app, but the phone’s main menu will revert to full color, which can be a shock if the screen brightness was increased to compensate for the darker red display.

Android phones offer several built-in methods to reduce screen brightness. Users can swipe down the notification panel to access a brightness slider and dim the screen. It is also recommended to disable adaptive brightness in the Display section of the settings. Some devices include an Extra Dim option in the Accessibility menu. Additionally, recent Samsung and Google Pixel models feature a Red Filter, often located under Accessibility, Vision Enhancements, and Color Filter, where users can select a color and adjust the opacity.

Apple iPhones also provide options to minimize the effect of white light. Users can swipe down from the top of the screen to find the vertical brightness slider, represented by a sun icon, and reduce the brightness to a comfortable level. Recent iPhones also include a color filter feature accessible through the Accessibility options. To apply it, users tap the Settings icon, select Accessibility, then Display & Text Size, and go to Color Filters. After tapping the Color Filter button, they can choose Color Tint and move the Hue and Intensity sliders all the way to the right.
summary: Bright smartphone screens bleach rhodopsin, a chemical essential for night vision that takes up to 30 minutes to build up in the dark. Users can mitigate this by enabling red light filters in stargazing apps or adjusting their phone's display settings.
