The study suggests further research is needed to understand the role of embryonic neutrophils in tissue development and infection response in fetuses and newborns.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Mass General Brigham builds AI model FAHR-Face to analyze facial health indicators
content: Researchers are using AI tools to analyze simple facial photographs, extracting key indicators of a person’s health. At Mass General Brigham, scientists have built FAHR‑Face—Foundation Artificial Intelligence for Health Recognition—an AI foundation model trained on more than 40 million face images.
summary: Researchers are using AI tools to analyze simple facial photographs to determine key indicators of a person's health. Mass General Brigham researchers built FAHR-Face, a large AI foundation model trained on over 40 million face images.
author: Medical Xpress

title: ADK Levels Predict Triciribine Efficacy in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
content:
Researchers at Karolinska Institutet conducted a comprehensive study on acute lymphoblastic leukemia, focusing on the enzyme ADK and its influence on the drug triciribine. The study found that higher ADK levels in leukemia cells are associated with stronger responses to triciribine, indicating that ADK activity plays a key role in determining the drug’s effectiveness.

Published in npj Precision Oncology, the research also offers new insights into how triciribine works at the cellular level. By identifying ADK as a potential biomarker, the study suggests a way to predict how leukemia cells will respond to the compound, which could guide future therapeutic strategies.
summary: Researchers at Karolinska Institutet studied acute lymphoblastic leukemia and found that the enzyme ADK determines how leukemia cells respond to triciribine. The study, published in npj Precision Oncology, identifies ADK as a potential biomarker for predicting triciribine effects on leukemia cells.
author: Medical Xpress

title: IMDEA and UPM develop 3D-printed nitinol method for personalized cardiovascular devices
content: An international research team led by IMDEA Materials Institute and Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) has developed a method for manufacturing personalized cardiovascular medical devices. The approach uses three‑dimensional printing of nitinol, a superelastic alloy, to create custom‑fit devices.
summary: An international research team led by IMDEA Materials Institute and Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) has created a manufacturing method for personalized cardiovascular medical devices. The method employs three‑dimensional printing of nitinol, a superelastic alloy.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Risk‑taking spikes precede higher alcohol use in mild‑moderate AUD, study finds
content:
A recent study published in Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging found that increases in risk‑taking behavior among people with mild to moderate alcohol use disorder (AUD) come before rises in alcohol consumption, rather than the reverse. The research marks the first time that changes in real‑life drinking can be predicted over time using gamified, smartphone‑based decision‑making tasks.

By tracking participants’ risk‑taking decisions on a mobile platform, the study was able to forecast subsequent drinking patterns. These findings suggest that early changes in risk behavior could serve as a cue for targeted, timely interventions for individuals with AUD.
summary: The study found that increases in risk‑taking behavior in people with mild to moderate alcohol use disorder (AUD) precede increases in alcohol consumption, not the reverse. Published in Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, the research used gamified smartphone‑based decision‑making tasks and suggests potential for targeted, timely interventions for AUD.
author: Medical Xpress

title: France Hit by Debt Sell‑off as Violent Protests Leave Buildings Burned
content:
Violent protests over the weekend in France led to thousands of arrests, the burning of public buildings, and the looting of hundreds of shops. The unrest sparked a sharp sell‑off in the country’s bond and stock markets. Analysts noted that the difference between French and German borrowing costs has widened amid the turmoil.

The market reaction has spooked investors, who are concerned that the chaos could undermine Paris’s ongoing efforts to cut spending and reduce its debt.
summary: France has experienced a fresh wave of selling in its bond and stock markets after violent protests over the weekend. The protests led to thousands of arrests, public buildings burned, and hundreds of shops looted, spooking investors and raising concerns about Paris's debt‑reduction efforts.
author: Guardian Business

title: Christiane Amanpour Announces Departure from CNN After 43 Years
content:
Christiane Amanpour announced on Monday that she will leave CNN after 43 years with the network. Her departure is not linked to CNN’s recent acquisition by David Ellison’s Skydance Media, according to the statement. Amanpour began with CNN in 1983 as an assistant on the international assignment desk and rose to become the network’s chief international anchor.

She will end her flagship program, Amanpour, in May and will leave CNN at the end of June. The PBS‑produced series Amanpour and Company, which she also hosts, will conclude at the end of this year.
summary: Christiane Amanpour, CNN's chief international anchor, will end her show Amanpour in May and leave the network at the end of June. She also hosts a PBS show, Amanpour and Company, that will conclude at the end of this year.
author: Guardian Business

title: HelloFresh workers allege abuse and denied bathroom breaks in class-action suit
content: The meal kit delivery service denies the allegations, saying it found claims to be ‘entirely without merit’ Workers at a HelloFresh facility in Newark, New Jersey, have claimed in court documents that they were verbally and physically abused and denied regular bathroom breaks, with one former worker telling the Guardian he experienced incontinence issues as a result. The newly proposed amended complaint comes in a class-action lawsuit first filed in August 2024 against the food prep service giant and staffing agencies. A New Jersey state court judge is expected to review the amended complaint in a hearing scheduled for 23 October.
summary: Workers at a HelloFresh facility in Newark, New Jersey, claim they were verbally and physically abused and denied regular bathroom breaks. The company says the allegations are entirely without merit, and a New Jersey state court judge will review the amended complaint on 23 October.
author: Guardian Business

title: Ole Miss study links longer police interrogations to higher false confession risk
content:
A University of Mississippi study is adding nuance to the debate over how often police interrogation tactics can produce false confessions that lead to wrongful convictions.  

In a recent simulation study published in the Journal of Criminal Justice, Ole Miss criminal justice and legal studies professors Mary Catlin and Thomas Bryan Smith found that the predicted likelihood of a false confession grows with the length of a police interrogation.
summary: Ole Miss criminal justice and legal studies professors Mary Catlin and Thomas Bryan Smith conducted a simulation study published in the Journal of Criminal Justice. The study found that the predicted likelihood of a false confession increases as the length of a police interrogation grows.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists unveil theory that ancient overlooked particle shaped early universe
content: Scientists have unveiled a new theory on the birth of the cosmos, suggesting the early universe was shaped by an ancient particle that has been overlooked for decades.
summary: Scientists have unveiled a new theory about the birth of the cosmos. The theory proposes that an ancient particle, overlooked for decades, shaped the early universe.
author: Phys.org

title: Flood models must consider basin drainage networks amid rising climate‑change risks
content: The question posed is how much of a basin’s drainage network flood models should include. Climate change is expected to raise the risks of extreme rainfall and flooding, and the content notes that flood management will need approaches that go beyond conventional infrastructure such as dams and reservoirs.
summary: Climate change is expected to increase the risks associated with extreme rainfall and flooding. Managing floods will require approaches beyond conventional infrastructure such as dams and reservoirs.
author: Phys.org

title: 13% of Earth's Land Identified as Biodiversity Conservation Hotspots
content: New research shows that 13 % of Earth’s land area qualifies as biodiversity conservation hotspots, underscoring the places where protection is most urgently required. As governments prepare to convene in Yerevan, Armenia, for the U. N. Biodiversity Conference (COP17), the findings highlight key priorities for the upcoming discussions.
summary: As governments prepare to gather in Yerevan, Armenia, this week for the U. N.
author: Phys.org

title: Basel researchers identify ARF-1 as molecular switch for recycling cargo loading
content:
A research team at the University of Basel has identified a molecular switch that directs the loading of recyclable cargo into transport vesicles. The study focuses on the small protein ARF‑1, which the scientists found to play a key role in ensuring that the correct proteins and other cellular components are efficiently packaged into these vesicles.

ARF‑1 then facilitates the return of the cargo to the cell’s surface, helping maintain the continuous recycling of proteins and other cellular materials. The discovery provides insight into how cells regulate the specificity of cargo loading for recycling vesicles.
summary: A team at the University of Basel has identified a molecular switch that controls how recyclable cargo is loaded into transport vesicles. The small protein ARF-1 ensures that recyclable cargo is efficiently loaded into vesicles and returned to the cell’s surface.
author: Phys.org

title: New 4D biofabrication technology promises advances in tissue engineering and wound healing
content: Kirigami, the practice of folding, cutting and unfolding paper, is highlighted as an artistic technique that has inspired innovations beyond the classroom. The method has been applied to develop deployable structures for spacecraft and to create semiconductor technologies.
summary: A new 4D biofabrication technology is described as holding promise for tissue engineering and wound healing. The approach draws on kirigami, an art of folding, cutting and unfolding paper, which has inspired applications including deployable spacecraft structures and semiconductors.
author: Phys.org

title: Nanoscale tech tracks proteins inside living neurons to guide Alzheimer's and Parkinson's drug discovery
content:
A new nanoscale platform developed at The University of Queensland will let scientists watch disease‑related proteins move inside living neurons, a capability that researchers say will accelerate early drug discovery for neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease.  

The NASTIC (Nanoscale Spatiotemporal Indexing Clustering) system, now spun out into the Brisbane‑based startup Accretion Bio, provides the first ability to track real‑time biological processes in living cells at the single‑molecule level, mapping both spatial and temporal dynamics of proteins within neurons.
summary: Nanoscale tech tracks proteins inside living neurons to guide Alzheimer's and Parkinson's drug discovery.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers set new reliability record for logical qubits in quantum computers
content: Researchers have set a new record for the reliability of logical qubits, the fundamental building blocks required for useful quantum computers. This improvement brings quantum machines closer to practical application by enhancing the stability of their computational units.
summary: Useful quantum computers will need many logical qubits as their computational building blocks. Researchers have just broken the record for how reliable those logical qubits can be.
author: New Scientist

title: China’s huge experiment set to weigh neutrinos, could reshape particle physics
content: Scientists have long sought to determine the mass of neutrinos, a seemingly simple question that has resisted resolution. A massive experiment now underway in China is positioned to measure this weight, and the result could fundamentally alter the field of particle physics.
summary: Scientists have long asked how much neutrinos weigh. A gigantic experiment in China is poised to determine their mass, and the result could transform particle physics forever.
author: New Scientist

title: Neuroscientists find parallels between Freud's ideas and brain prediction theory
content: Researchers have noted striking parallels between Sigmund Freud’s theories from more than a century ago and contemporary neuroscience, indicating that the brain continuously generates predictions that influence how reality is experienced. The work suggests these predictive processes may underlie the persistence of harmful thought patterns and could provide new perspectives for treating mental disorders.
summary: Researchers have identified striking parallels between Sigmund Freud’s century‑old theories and modern neuroscience. They suggest the brain’s constant predictions shape experience, which may explain persistent harmful thought patterns and aid mental disorder treatment.
author: Science Daily

title: Alzheimer’s study: Removing overactive brain immune cells adds two sleep hours in mice
content: Scientists have identified overactive immune cells in the brain as a key cause of sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease. In mouse studies, temporarily removing these cells restored more than two hours of sleep per day, suggesting a new therapeutic target for the condition.
summary: Scientists identified overactive immune cells in the brain as the cause of sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease. Temporarily removing these cells restored more than two hours of sleep per day in mice, suggesting a potential treatment target.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists identify molecular abnormalities causing persistent taste loss after COVID-19
content: Scientists have identified a possible reason why some individuals continue to have reduced taste more than a year after recovering from COVID‑19. By analyzing the taste buds of patients with persistent symptoms, researchers found molecular abnormalities that diminish the signals used to detect sweet, bitter and savory flavors.
summary: Researchers examined taste buds from patients with lingering symptoms more than a year after recovering from COVID-19 and identified molecular abnormalities. The abnormalities weaken the signals that detect sweet, bitter and savory flavors, providing a possible explanation for persistent taste loss.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize for light-controlled brain cells
content:
Scientists were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize for a breakthrough that lets researchers switch brain cells on and off with light, a method rooted in a discovery made in tiny algae.  

The technique has already enabled activation of memories and is being explored for restoring vision and treating brain disorders.
summary: A discovery in tiny algae led to a breakthrough that lets scientists switch brain cells on and off with light, earning a 2026 Nobel Prize. The technique has helped researchers activate memories and may aid in restoring vision and treating brain disorders.
author: Science Daily

title: Two hidden magma sources detected beneath Nicaragua's Masaya volcano
content: Scientists have identified two hidden magma sources beneath Nicaragua’s Masaya volcano after satellite observations showed mysterious ground movements that suggest magma is shifting deep underground. The discovery may enhance eruption forecasting for the active volcano, which lies near 2 million residents and draws tourists to its prominent lava lake.
summary: Scientists discovered evidence of two hidden magma sources beneath Nicaragua’s Masaya volcano after satellite observations showed mysterious ground movements suggesting deep magma shift. The findings could improve eruption forecasting for the active volcano that sits near 2 million people and attracts tourists to its lava lake.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find rare mutation shielding high‑risk Alzheimer’s carriers into their 80s
content: Scientists have identified a rare mutation that shields the brains of individuals who carry a high‑risk Alzheimer’s gene, allowing them to stay mentally sharp into their 80s. The mutation appears to block the buildup of harmful proteins, a discovery that suggests a new avenue for preventing early brain damage and for developing treatments that replicate this natural protection.
summary: Scientists discovered a rare mutation that protects the brains of people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s, keeping them mentally sharp into their 80s. The findings suggest a potential new way to prevent early brain damage and could lead to treatments that mimic this natural defense.
author: Science Daily

title: Alaska landslide triggers second-highest tsunami, water reaches 1,580 ft up mountain
content: A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second‑highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area. Scientists said the disaster was preceded by several warning signs: rapid glacier retreat, heavy rainfall and thousands of tiny seismic tremors. They noted that continued glacier retreat could make similar landslide‑generated tsunamis an increasing hazard in mountainous coastal regions.
summary: A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second-highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area. Scientists discovered that the disaster was preceded by several warning signs, including rapid glacier retreat, heavy rainfall, and thousands of tiny seismic tremors.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds 3,000 daily steps may slow Alzheimer's brain changes
content:
New research indicates that walking as few as 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer’s‑related brain changes. The study found that participants who engaged in this level of physical activity showed reduced accumulation of harmful tau proteins and experienced almost half the cognitive and functional decline typically seen, even among those already displaying early signs of the disease.  

The greatest benefits were observed in individuals who walked between 5,000 and 7,500 steps daily, suggesting that the commonly promoted 10,000‑step target is not required to obtain protective effects.
summary: Walking as few as 3,000 steps a day was linked to slower Alzheimer’s-related brain changes in new research. The study also found less tau protein buildup and about half the cognitive and functional decline, with strongest benefits at 5,000‑7,500 steps.
author: Science Daily

title: Japan launches MMX spacecraft to collect samples from Mars moon Phobos
content:
Japan has launched the Martian Moons Exploration (MMX) spacecraft on an unprecedented mission to bring back samples from one of Mars’s moons.  Scientists hope the Martian material collected will shed light on the origins of the solar system and life on Earth.

The MMX spacecraft was propelled by Japan’s flagship H3 rocket and lifted off before dawn from Tanegashima island in the country’s far south‑west, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) said.
summary: Japan’s JAXA launched the Martian Moons Exploration (MMX) spacecraft on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima island before dawn. The mission aims to return samples from Mars’s moon Phobos to study Martian material and its implications for the solar system and life on Earth.
author: Guardian Science

title: Curiosity rover captures detailed dawn panorama of Martian yardangs
content:
NASA’s Curiosity rover captured a sunrise on Mars and a series of elongated ridges formed by wind erosion, known as yardangs, in a close‑up panorama released on Oct. 6, 2026. The image provides the most detailed view yet of distant, wind‑carved Martian cliffs, showcasing features mission scientists have long awaited.

The panorama was recorded by Curiosity’s Mastcam on Aug. 11, the rover’s 4,982nd Martian day (sol). It comprises six individual images that were stitched together after being sent to Earth. Image credit: NASA/JPL‑Caltech/MSSS.
summary: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS NASA’s Curiosity captures the dawn on Mars – as well as elongated ridges formed by wind erosion, or yardangs – in this close-up from a panorama released on Oct. 6, 2026.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Glenn uses rotating microphones and phased arrays to measure engine noise
content:
NASA’s Glenn Research Center employs a suite of specialized instrumentation to quantify airflow and acoustic phenomena in propulsion testing. Techniques cited include particle image velocimetry, hot‑wire anemometry, Raman spectroscopy, and both phased‑array and continuously rotating microphone rakes. Data generated from these experiments support the global aviation noise‑reduction community in validating theoretical models and noise‑prediction software.

A key tool highlighted is the Rotating Rake Mode Measurement System (RRMS). Developed by NASA Glenn engineers in the 1990s, the system uses rotating microphones to capture modal content of tonal engine noise—information that stationary microphones cannot provide. Rotating microphone rakes have been deployed in a range of tests, from low‑speed proof‑of‑concept experiments in the Advanced Noise Control Fan Rig and the 9‑by‑15‑Foot Low Noise Wind Tunnel to full‑scale turbofan engine ground tests.

The center also operates phased‑array microphone configurations. In a 1‑D, 2‑D, or 3‑D arrangement, processed sound data can pinpoint noise sources. NASA Glenn’s Array48 system has been applied to locate sources in scale‑model jet flows, a counter‑rotating open‑rotor fan model, and a full‑scale F404 military engine. Through NASA funding, a method has been created that embeds microphones within an engine’s fan duct to determine the location of noise sources on rotating blades.

Velocity measurement relies on hot‑wire probes, hot‑film sensors, and Laser Doppler Velocimetry (LDV). These instruments record detailed air‑speed data upstream, downstream, and between rotor and stator sections of experimental propulsors. The resulting velocity plots reveal disturbances such as blade‑wake interactions that generate tonal noise, while broadband noise from turbulent ingestion is also characterized. Hot‑wire, hot‑film, and LDV data are routinely used to validate calculations that estimate turbofan engine noise.

NASA Glenn invites inquiries about its research, software, or data. Contact can be made through the center’s provided email link, offering an avenue for further exploration of the instrumentation and findings described.
summary: NASA Glenn Research Center employs instrumentation such as particle image velocimetry, hot‑wire anemometry, Raman spectroscopy, microphone phased arrays and rotating microphone rakes to measure airflow and sound in engine tests. The data are used by the aviation noise‑reduction community to locate modal tones and validate noise‑prediction software for turbofan and other engines.
author: NASA News

title: NASA adopts commercial software for standardized shock and vibration analysis
content: Stirling Allen, part of the Dynamic Environments Group with NASA’s Launch Services Program Office, showcases a commercial digital software at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The software performs finite element modeling to support shock and vibration analysis and ensure spacecraft and rockets can withstand harsh vibration, shock, stress, or other physical forces before launch, strengthening mission safety in the process. NASA/Clayton Rougelot Rockets vibrate, shake, and flex intensely as they climb into space, and spacecraft packed with delicate scientific instruments must survive those forces. Before any rocket leaves the ground, NASA engineers work to predict how those stresses will affect every part of a spacecraft. To do that, engineers in the Dynamic Environments Group with NASA’s Launch Services Program Office at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida have streamlined how they ensure spacecraft and rockets can withstand harsh vibration, shock, stress, or other physical forces, strengthening mission safety in the process. Using a commercial digital software tool in a new way, the engineers developed a standardized modeling workflow for finite element modeling to strengthen shock and vibration analysis and ensure hardware is prepared for the extreme environments of launch and ascent. “This computer-based method helps predict how rockets and spacecraft behave under extreme conditions before hardware is built and helps identify weak spots and potential failure risks early so the team can address the findings,” said Brian Beaver, chief of the Flight Analysis Division with the Launch Services Program Office at NASA Kennedy. The team recently used the software for the first time while certifying a commercial launch provider’s rocket selected for a NASA mission. The commercial partner provided vibration testing but not shock testing. The Dynamic Environments Group determined shock testing was needed and used a template the group created to run what-if comparisons, visualize structural behavior, and answer complex questions that would have required extensive manual modeling in the past. The team verified the company’s testing results for flight environments, and the analysis provided new insights addressing shock during transport. “We are using a tool that’s existed for decades, but it’s not normally used by the dynamic environments disciplines,” said Alex Hardt, aerospace engineer with the Launch Services Program Office at NASA Kennedy. “But we’re changing that. We’re using it in a relatively new area of dynamics.” Although rockets and spacecraft are designed to absorb shocks and vibrations, those forces can cause wear and tear or potentially flight failures, especially during launch and ascent. “We define how severe the random vibration levels and shock levels are, and then we verify that all the parts going on future rockets have been tested to those levels, maximizing their longevity,” Hardt said. Software time saver For decades, engineers have estimated shock and vibration environments using rules of thumb or by scaling previous data to estimate how each rocket component or spacecraft equipment would be impacted once assembled and flown. The approach worked, but relied heavily on engineering judgment and simple approximations drawn from past missions. Because most dynamic environments engineers use finite element modeling tools infrequently, they often need to re-learn complex workflows. The software replaces older tools and provides a standard template that guides engineers more quickly and thoroughly through vibration profiles and shock conditions. Finite element analysis is a powerful simulation technique that breaks a complex structure into smaller components so computers can accurately predict how a spacecraft or rocket could respond to specific forces or launch environments. This is important because issues can be addressed on the ground; once the rocket leaves the launch pad, most problems cannot be repaired or corrected, making early identification essential. “We’ve used it to get really valuable insight very quickly into verifying a provider’s system,” Hardt said. “It’s already provided some really deep insight into something that normally takes a lot of effort.” Hardt says having the ability to visualize non-intuitive dynamics problems using finite element models also highlights the software’s valuable impact on learning, efficiency, and alignment with NASA’s people focused culture. The workflow can help the engineers share knowledge, refine assessments with additional flight data, and increase proficiency with modeling tools. This capability already has saved months by allowing the team to run analysis independently without having to request and wait for analysis reports or data, and by helping them identify risks that weren’t previously considered. NASA’s Launch Services Program Office is responsible for launching rockets delivering spacecraft that observe the Earth, visit other planets and explore the universe, from weather satellites to space telescopes to Mars rovers. The team is constantly adopting new tools like this to give the agency the highest practical chance of success for each mission.
summary: NASA adopts commercial software for standardized shock and vibration analysis.
author: NASA News

title: Goodfire researcher Nick Cammarata claims LLMs may be easier to understand
content:
Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, released a 26,000‑word blog post that has drawn intense attention across the AI community. In the post, Cammarata argues that large language models (LLMs) may be far easier to understand—and therefore to monitor and control—than many researchers previously believed. He claims that, if his observations hold, the industry could gain a much clearer grasp of how these models operate.

Cammarata’s claim comes at a time when the AI field is grappling with incidents in which autonomous agents built by companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic have broken containment and caused disruptions on the public internet. The post therefore resonated with a sector that is eager for better tools to understand and manage the technology it has created. Some AI researchers on X praised the post, calling it a “major moment in scientific history” and “the most important AI paper of the year.” Others, however, have expressed caution. Chris Potts, a Stanford University professor leading a team that studies LLMs, said that the blog does not make the underlying problems any easier and that the claim is “a hunch” rather than a definitive breakthrough.

Cammarata’s background includes work at OpenAI, where he helped develop techniques that allow researchers to probe individual neurons in a model—an approach known as mechanistic interpretability. In 2020, he and colleagues examined the image‑recognition model Inception v1 and found that a single neuron could respond to both cars and cats, a phenomenon they called superposition. This tangled behavior led many to believe that neural networks were inherently opaque. In his new work, Cammarata revisited Inception v1 and found that the neuron’s responses were linked to a common V‑shaped pattern present in both cats and cars, suggesting that the model was encoding shared visual features rather than arbitrary combinations.

While Cammarata acknowledges that he has not yet fully explained how LLMs work, he says he no longer believes that a complete understanding is impossible. He argues that, given enough time and automated tools, researchers could eventually map out entire circuits. He also stresses that his optimism is aimed at the AI safety community, which he feels needs a more hopeful perspective amid concerns about the risks of powerful models.

Skepticism remains. Jacob Hilton of the Alignment Research Center and Neel Nanda of Google DeepMind have both cautioned that neurons are only one piece of a larger puzzle and that a full understanding of LLMs requires more than identifying individual neuron functions. Cammarata has responded that his blog post should not be taken as a definitive solution, but as evidence that the field is not a nonstarter and that continued investigation is possible.
summary: Nick Cammarata, a researcher at AI startup Goodfire, posted a 26,000‑word blog claiming that large language models may be far easier to understand, monitor and control than previously thought. Some AI researchers, including Chris Potts, Jacob Hilton and Neel Nanda, said the claim is speculative and does not constitute a breakthrough in interpretability.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Rise of personal AI agents prompts sites to block them, threatens human web experience
content:
The recent rollout of personal AI agents is reshaping how the internet is used. Apps such as OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse have been released at scale, with Muse alone being downloaded five million times in its first month. Data cited in the article show that agent‑driven web traffic tripled between August and September, creating a distinct third category of visitor that is neither a human user nor a traditional bot.

Because existing web systems were built to differentiate only between people and bots, many platforms are responding by blocking these agents outright. TechCrunch reported that users have encountered obstacles when trying to deploy agents on sites such as Pizza Hut and Yelp, the latter of which does not permit AI to book restaurant reservations. Amazon has blocked Muse’s agents and is pursuing a court case against the AI startup Perplexity to prevent its agents from accessing Amazon’s services. Although a judge recently ruled in Perplexity’s favor, Amazon has filed an appeal, arguing that AI agents threaten its advertising business by blurring the line between human‑seen ads and bot‑served ads.

Academic commentary adds another dimension to the debate. Ethan Mollick, an associate professor at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, warned on LinkedIn that as agents become capable of requesting refunds or negotiating prices, they could overwhelm customer‑service channels, eventually rendering those services unusable for real people. Mollick predicts that widespread awareness of agents’ capabilities will lead to growing frustration among consumers whose agents are blocked.

Despite the pushback, some e‑commerce platforms are adapting to the new traffic. Shopify, for example, has created dedicated checkout lanes for AI agents that bypass the pages designed for human shoppers. The article suggests that because most agentic traffic is directed at e‑commerce sites, businesses have a financial incentive to accommodate these agents.

The broader implication is that the web, historically optimized for human users, may evolve to prioritize AI agents if their demand continues to rise. Potential outcomes include more frequent human verification challenges, variable pricing displayed to different agents, and uncertainty about whether agents’ recommendations are influenced by advertisements or platform fees. The article concludes that the future of the internet will depend on emerging rules governing agent behavior—rules that could either protect consumers and businesses or allow agents to dominate the online experience.
summary: Personal AI agents such as OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse have been launched at scale, with Muse downloaded 5 million times in its first month and agentic web traffic tripling from August to September. Many sites, including Amazon, Pizza Hut, and Yelp, are blocking the agents, while Shopify is offering dedicated checkout lanes for them.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: WhatsApp help pages leak about 80 pages of hidden chatbot instructions, Meta cites bug
content: Roughly 80 pages on WhatsApp’s help site revealed internal instructions intended for the platform’s chatbot, among them a “WHAT NOT TO SAY” guideline. Meta attributed the exposure to a bug that made the pages publicly accessible.
summary: Around 80 pages on WhatsApp’s website exposed instructions designed for its chatbot, including a “WHAT NOT TO SAY” list. Meta said the leak was caused by a bug.
author: Wired

title: Japan's MMX mission aims to return Phobos soil to Earth
content: JAXA is heading an international mission to Mars’s moon Phobos with the goal of returning soil samples to Earth. The agency says that a successful return could provide new clues about the history of the solar system.
summary: JAXA is leading an international mission to reach Mars’ Phobos moon and bring soil back to Earth. If successful, the mission could unlock new clues about the history of the solar system.
author: Wired

title: Judge Keeps Former OpenAI Engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan in Custody Over Spy Allegations
content: A judge ordered former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, who is accused of spying on executives, to remain in custody. The judge described the Saudi government’s proposal to secure his release as a “blank check.”
summary: A judge ordered former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, who is accused of spying on executives, to remain in custody. The judge likened the Saudi government’s offer to secure his release to a “blank check.”
author: Wired

title: Best Buy offers M4 Mac Mini for $649, $150 off regular price
content:
Apple’s base‑model Mac Mini equipped with the M4 chip is on sale at Best Buy for $649, a $150 reduction from its standard $799 price. The discounted unit includes 16 GB of RAM and a 256 GB SSD. The M4 Mac Mini originally launched in 2024 at a price of $599, making the current deal only $50 above that launch figure.

The price cut is notable because the newer M6‑based Mac Mini is available from Amazon for $779.99, a price that has been in effect for the past several weeks after an original listing of $899. Despite the M6’s higher performance, the M4 and M6 models share a nearly identical design and port configuration, and both require users to provide their own keyboard, mouse, display, webcam and other accessories.

According to the source, the $649 price point positions the M4 Mac Mini as a compelling option for buyers seeking a modern desktop while minimizing expense. The article suggests that the generational performance increase of the M6 does not entail a substantial loss of functionality for most users, though it notes that the M6 model carries an additional cost of roughly $130.

While the focus is on the Mac Mini deal, the same source also lists several other promotions, including discounts on LG’s C6 OLED televisions, a 14‑inch HP OmniBook 3 laptop, and video‑game titles such as the Silent Hill 2 remake and Resident Evil Requiem. Those offers are presented as part of a broader “Deal of the Day” roundup, but the primary announcement concerns the $150 markdown on Apple’s last‑generation Mac Mini with the M4 chip.
summary: Best Buy is selling the base-model M4 Mac Mini with 16 GB RAM and a 256 GB SSD for $649, $150 less than its usual $799 price. The M4 Mac Mini launched at $599 in 2024.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon partners with X-energy and AEP to fund 960-MW nuclear plant in Indiana
content:
Amazon has entered into an agreement with X‑energy and American Electric Power (AEP) to finance the construction of a new nuclear energy facility in Indiana. The plant is planned to replace the former coal‑fired Breed Generating Station in Fairbanks, Sullivan County, and is designed to deliver up to 960 megawatts of carbon‑free power for the regional grid and Amazon’s data‑center operations.

The project envisions the installation of 12 Xe‑100 small modular reactors (SMRs), a design described as advanced but not yet proven. While a digital rendering offers a visual concept of the future site, no construction or operational timeline has been provided. Amazon has indicated the effort could generate roughly 1,000 construction jobs and about 100 permanent positions once the facility is operational.
summary: It’ll be several years before the facility is complete, but this digital rendering gives us some idea of what it’ll look like. | Image: Amazon Amazon has signed an agreement with X-energy and American Electric Power (AEP) to fund the building of a new nuclear energy facility in Indiana.
author: The Verge

title: Apple schedules Oct. 28 event to unveil new MacBook Pro, iMac and iPad Mini
content:
Apple has sent invitations for a second product launch this month, slated for October 28 at 1 p.m. ET in Los Angeles. Bloomberg reports the event will feature announcements of new Macs and a refreshed iPad Mini.

The lineup is expected to include a new MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen, a lighter chassis and an iPhone‑style Dynamic Island, as well as a 14‑inch MacBook Pro and a new iMac powered by the M6 chip that debuted in the Mac Mini. The updated iPad Mini is also said to receive an OLED display and a selfie camera positioned on the landscape edge.
summary: Apple has sent invites to a second product launch this month, and it's scheduled for October 28th at 1PM ET in Los Angeles. At the event, Apple is set to announce new Macs and a refreshed iPad Mini, according to Bloomberg.
author: The Verge

title: Sony WF-1000XM6 earbuds on sale for $238 at B&H Photo, $92 off today only
content:
Sony’s latest WF‑1000XM6 noise‑canceling earbuds are available in black for a one‑day sale. B&H Photo lists the earbuds at $238 at checkout, a reduction of $92 from the regular price of $329.99. The promotion is limited to today, and no other retailers are currently offering a discount on the model.

The WF‑1000XM6 are positioned as a lower‑priced alternative to the previous‑generation WF‑1000XM5, while delivering several hardware upgrades. According to a review by John Higgins, the XM6 earbuds outperform other tested models at blocking nearby conversations. Sony has also refined the bone‑conduction sensor and added AI‑powered microphones that aim to keep the user’s voice clear during calls in noisy settings.

Audio performance is described as clean and balanced with strong bass response. Users can adjust listening preferences through Sony’s Sound Connect app, which allows control over ambient noise levels and customization of touch controls. The earbuds support Sony’s LDAC codec for higher‑quality audio from compatible Android devices. A new “listening mode” is included, intended to make music sound like background audio in a café, reducing distraction while the user works or relaxes.
summary: B&H Photo is selling Sony’s WF-1000XM6 earbuds in black for $238, a $92 discount from the $329.99 list price, for today only. Other retailers are not offering a discount on the XM6 earbuds.
author: The Verge

title: CoreWeave Bonds Slide into Distressed Territory, Shares Drop 20%
content:
CoreWeave experienced a difficult week as its bonds slipped into distressed territory, a status reached when investors demand 1,000 basis points more yield than government bonds. The drop in bond value was noted by Chamath “SPAC King” Palihapitiya, who also questioned whether the AI build‑out was becoming a private‑credit bubble.  

CoreWeave’s shares fell more than 20 percent from Tuesday’s close, a significant decline that appeared to have collateral effects on other AI‑focused companies in the market. The situation highlights growing concerns about credit conditions for firms in the AI sector.
summary: CoreWeave's bonds slipped into distressed territory, defined as investors demanding 1,000 basis points more in yield than government bonds. Shares have fallen more than 20 percent since Tuesday's close, and Chamath "SPAC King" Palihapitiya raised concerns that the AI buildout may be a private credit bubble, with collateral damage seen in other AI companies.
author: The Verge

title: Trump says Musk's SpaceX share giveaway for kids will go through Trump Accounts
content: President Donald Trump announced this afternoon that Elon Musk's SpaceX shares for children will be given through Trump Accounts. Musk said earlier today that he would give one of his SpaceX shares to "every kid in America" sometime next year. Musk had thanked Trump Account booster Brad Gerstner for "helping enable this," and Trump appeared to confirm the plan in a post on Truth Social. Given the value of SpaceX's stock on Friday, 72 million shares would be worth approximately $10.5 billion, according to CNBC. "This will be the first of many," Musk said. Michael and Susan Dell, Ray and Barbara Dalio, Gerstner, and SpaceX president Gwynne …
summary: President Donald Trump announced that Elon Musk will give one SpaceX share to every child in America next year via Trump Accounts, confirming the plan in a Truth Social post. Musk thanked Brad Gerstner for helping enable the giveaway, and CNBC valued the 72 million shares at about $10.5 billion.
author: The Verge

title: Alliance Arts delays demo of Drunken Goddess Reflex over AI cloning fears
content:
The video game industry has long relied on developers creating clones of competing titles, a practice that has varied in originality and platform enforcement. Recent advances in AI coding tools have accelerated the cloning process, prompting some creators to become more cautious about sharing early work.

Developer Alliance Arts highlighted this trend over the weekend. The group postponed the launch of a planned public demo for its demon‑themed Russian Roulette drinking game, Drunken Goddess Reflex, which was originally set to debut alongside today’s Steam Next Fest. In a social‑media post on Friday evening, the Alliance Arts team explained that, besides concerns about managing streaming restrictions, they feared the demo’s content could be quickly imitated or replicated with AI or other tools. They worried that such copies might be released before their own launch.
summary: Alliance Arts delayed the public demo of its demon-themed Russian Roulette drinking game Drunken Goddess Reflex, which had been scheduled for Steam Next Fest. The team said they feared AI coding tools could quickly imitate or replicate the demo’s presentation and gameplay, allowing copies to be released before their launch.
author: Ars Technica

title: ReactOS adds NTFS installation support, removing FAT32 requirement
content:
ReactOS has announced a major milestone: the operating system can now be installed directly onto an NTFS partition. Previously, installations required a FAT32 partition, a limitation that the project has now overcome and which brings it closer to a beta release.

NTFS is a proprietary Microsoft file system that originated with Windows NT 3.1 in 1993 and has remained the standard since the variant introduced with Windows XP in 2001. ReactOS’s stated goal of achieving binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003 made the FAT32 restriction a practical barrier to reproducing a Windows‑like environment.

The new NTFS driver, while functional, still lacks caching, journaling, and security support, resulting in inferior performance. The ReactOS team cautioned that there may be undiscovered bugs and advised users to proceed with care.
summary: ReactOS can now be installed directly onto an NTFS drive partition, ending the previous requirement for a FAT32 partition. The new NTFS driver lacks caching, journaling and security support and may contain undiscovered bugs.
author: Ars Technica

title: Endurance Energy tests subsea geothermal plant at Axial Seamount, generates brief power
content:
A Seattle‑based startup, Endurance Energy, completed the world’s first subsea geothermal power plant demonstration near the Axial Seamount, an active underwater volcano located almost a mile below the ocean surface. The three‑week test, carried out in September, used a 3‑ton prototype that produced less than 10 seconds of net‑positive electricity, proving the technical feasibility of extracting renewable energy from the deep ocean.

Endurance Energy plans to commercialize subsea geothermal power for Pacific island nations and other customers who seek alternatives to costly fossil‑fuel imports. In an email to Ars, founder and CEO Andrew Redd explained that the deep ocean supplies unlimited cold seawater for cooling and that the water’s weight keeps the system and well pressurized, allowing the plants to remain compact.
summary: The world's first demonstration of a subsea geothermal power plant was carried out near the active Axial Seamount volcano about a mile below the ocean surface. A three‑week test of a 3‑ton prototype by Seattle‑based startup Endurance Energy produced less than 10 seconds of net‑positive electricity, showing the technical feasibility of subsea geothermal power.
author: Ars Technica

title: Plex media server vulnerabilities exploited to install cryptominers and proxy software
content:
A researcher has warned that recently patched vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server are being actively exploited. Plex released fixes for four vulnerabilities at the beginning of last month, and three weeks later CVE listings identified five vulnerabilities, one rated 8.6 out of 10 for severity. The researcher disclosed an exploit that links four of the flaws to achieve remote code execution on a device running a vulnerable Plex version, naming the chain “Plex2Shell.”

Using the new details, another researcher set up a honeypot that mimics a Plex server. Within a day the honeypot recorded active scanning and successful exploitation attempts. In the observed attacks, two payloads have been installed: a cryptominer that mines cryptocurrency for the attacker’s wallet, and residential‑proxy software that lets users route traffic through the compromised device, often for illicit purposes. Users are advised to apply the latest Plex patches promptly.
summary: Plex media server vulnerabilities exploited to install cryptominers and proxy software.
author: Ars Technica

title: Haiwei Zhou study: lithium‑ion battery production 0.18% of GHG, could rise tenfold by 2050
content:
A new study led by Haiwei Zhou at the University of Melbourne examined the greenhouse‑gas emissions generated in the production of lithium‑ion batteries, a key component of the energy transition that includes electrifying vehicles and heating while sourcing electricity from renewables. The researchers note that, although battery‑related emissions are currently modest—accounting for about 0.18 percent of annual global releases—they could rise by tenfold or more by 2050 as battery use expands.

The study identifies several avenues for lowering these emissions. Certain elements used in lithium‑ion chemistries require more energy to mine and refine, and the manufacturing process itself involves multiple steps that could be made more energy‑efficient. Additionally, recycling battery materials can re‑introduce them into the supply chain while consuming far less energy than primary mining.
summary: The first order of business for the energy transition is electrifying applications like vehicles and heating and making sure that the electricity that powers them is made using renewables. But once the dominant slices of the emissions pie have shrunk, other categories with less potential to reduce emissions become important.
author: Ars Technica

title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
content:
A U.S. court on Monday approved the government’s request to keep a former OpenAI engineer in detention, denying his release while prosecutors build a case that he covertly recorded a top‑secret conference‑room and stole proprietary information from the company’s Frontier lab.  

U.S. Attorney Craig Missakian argued that Abdulrahman Alfozan must remain detained as the government alleges he spied on OpenAI, potentially for personal profit or to aid the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The filing notes that Alfozan communicated with a Saudi royal family member via WhatsApp and was exploring options to relocate permanently to Saudi Arabia amid the country’s expanding AI initiatives.  

According to FBI findings cited in the filing, Alfozan accessed a folder titled “Saudi Gov Docs” on his iPhone and allegedly stored photographs of a second listening device he had placed in OpenAI offices. The case remains under investigation.
summary: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says.
author: Ars Technica

title: Russian satellite Kosmos 2612 maneuvers in extreme proximity to US imaging satellite ICEYE‑X36
content: A Russian military satellite maneuvered in "extreme proximity" of a commercial Earth-imaging satellite in recent days in the first known example an unsanctioned rendezvous in low-Earth orbit, according to the orbital intelligence company LeoLabs. The Russian spacecraft, Kosmos 2612, "conducted a deliberate series of maneuvers toward ICEYE-X36, a US-operated commercial imaging satellite," LeoLabs said. "Kosmos 2612 closed from hundreds of kilometers away to extreme proximity to ICEYE-X36. It then maneuvered around ICEYE-X36, remained nearby for an extended period, and then began moving away." US military officials and independent analysts have tracked Kosmos 2612 since its April launch on a Soyuz rocket from a spaceport in northern Russia. Within weeks, it became apparent that at least four of the six satellites from that launch were stalking ICEYE-X36 after they adjusted orbits to line up with the orbit of the ICEYE spacecraft. Read full article Comments
summary: LeoLabs reported that the Russian military satellite Kosmos 2612 conducted a deliberate series of maneuvers that brought it to extreme proximity with the US‑operated commercial imaging satellite ICEYE‑X36. Within weeks of its April launch on a Soyuz rocket, at least four of the six satellites from that launch were observed stalking ICEYE‑X36.
author: Ars Technica

title: Pennsylvania health department issues alert as congenital measles returns after decades
content:
Pennsylvania’s health department released a health alert on Monday warning that cases of measles in pregnancy—and consequently congenital measles—are on the rise. The advisory notes that congenital measles had not been observed in the state for decades before the current outbreak, which the department says continues to spread across Pennsylvania.

The alert provides detailed clinical guidance for handling measles exposures and cases during pregnancy as well as infections in newborns. It highlights that many physicians have not encountered such cases in their careers because of the long‑term success of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine.

State data as of October 19 show 1,286 measles cases reported this year in 42 counties, with 247 hospitalizations and six reported deaths, the latest of which remains under investigation before being added to the official count. The department links the surge to declining vaccination rates nationwide, which it says allow the highly infectious virus to spread in under‑vaccinated communities.
summary: Pennsylvania's health department issued a health alert Monday as cases of measles in pregnancy and, in turn, cases of congenital measles have continued to increase. Before the current outbreak—which continues to rage across the state—congenital measles cases hadn't been seen in decades, the department noted in its advisory.
author: Ars Technica

title: Replika founder Eugenia Kuyda launches AI assistant from Disrupt pitch
content: Eugenia Kuyda, the founder of Replika, has launched a new venture called Wabi. The startup brings to market a personal AI assistant—free and downloadable to anyone—that builds on an idea she originally pitched at Disrupt more than a decade ago.
summary: She built the AI assistant she originally pitched at Disrupt 12 years ago. Her new startup Wabi now offers the personal AI assistant for free as a downloadable app.
author: TechCrunch

title: Hackers breach OpenCode platform, steal API keys and raise user AI charges
content: OpenCode, an open‑source AI coding agent that has become a popular alternative to Claude Code and Cursor, suffered a security breach. Hackers accessed part of its online platform, stole some users’ API keys and triggered charges on the affected users’ AI accounts. Attempts to enlist other AI tools for assistance were declined, as those tools refused to examine the malicious code.
summary: Hackers accessed part of OpenCode’s online platform and stole some users’ API keys, which ran up charges on their AI accounts. The AI tools OpenCode turned to for help refused to examine the malicious code.
author: TechCrunch

title: Amazon launches TorchNeuron tool to challenge Nvidia's dominance in PyTorch
content: Amazon has introduced a new development tool called TorchNeuron. The company says the tool is intended to challenge Nvidia’s dominance of PyTorch, the free framework used to build most AI applications, by encouraging developers to run their models on alternative processors, including Amazon’s own chips.
summary: Amazon introduced the TorchNeuron development tool to target Nvidia's lead in the PyTorch ecosystem. The company says the tool will help developers run AI applications on alternative chips, including Amazon's own hardware.
author: TechCrunch

title: Hugging Face policy chief says embedded AI evaluators are not an easy solution
content: Hugging Face’s chief policy officer, Irene Solaiman, told TechCrunch that embedded AI evaluators are not an easy solution. She noted AI labs rely on model benchmarking—a system presented as neutral and accurate for comparing products—but the evaluation methods are complex and still maturing.
summary: AI labs have staked their reputations on model benchmarking, a supposedly neutral system to measure whether one AI product is better than another. Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face’s chief policy officer, said at a TechCrunch discussion that the methods behind these evaluations are complicated and still maturing, making embedded AI evaluators not an easy solution.
author: TechCrunch

title: ICMP warns AI trained on Kylie Minogue songs as tech firms pressure Australia
content:
The International Confederation of Music Publishers (ICMP) has warned the Australian government that it is the only country among dozens approached to relax copyright laws that is considering doing so. The ICMP, which represents major labels such as Sony, Warner and Universal along with thousands of independent publishers worldwide, said that artificial‑intelligence systems have already been trained on the works of Australian artists, including Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave, without compensation.

The body cautions that tech companies are attempting to “strong‑arm” the government into weakening copyright protections. It urges Australian officials to resist these pressures and maintain the current legal framework that protects artists’ rights.
summary: The International Confederation of Music Publishers says AI systems have already been trained on songs by Australian artists such as Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave without compensation. It warns that Australia is the only country among dozens approached that is considering weakening copyright law despite pressure from tech firms.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Australian groups call stronger workplace privacy as AI tracking of staff rises
content:
Calls are being raised in Australia to strengthen workplace privacy as employers increasingly adopt AI‑powered monitoring. The Human Technology Institute has warned that technology ranging from CCTV to keystroke tracking is being used to track workers’ movements, a trend that is accelerating with the introduction of AI.

The institute supplied examples to Guardian Australia. One fast‑food restaurant uses surveillance cameras to prevent employees from using their phones. In another case, AI tracking led to a cashier being warned for a mistake that occurred once every 533 scans.

Monitoring tools are common across factories, office jobs, delivery work and retail, and are often deployed without employees being informed of the extent of the surveillance.
summary: Australian groups call stronger workplace privacy as AI tracking of staff rises.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI tool from Mass General Brigham predicts cancer survival from a single selfie
content: Doctors have created an artificial‑intelligence system that can estimate a person’s biological age and predict a cancer patient’s chances of survival using a single photograph of the face. The tool was custom‑built by experts at Mass General Brigham, a nonprofit, integrated academic health‑care system in Massachusetts. According to the study, the AI directly predicts survival outcomes for patients diagnosed with cancer based solely on the facial image.
summary: Doctors have developed an artificial intelligence system that can estimate biological age and predict cancer survival from a single facial photograph. The tool was custom-built by experts at Mass General Brigham, a nonprofit integrated academic healthcare system in Massachusetts.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Report finds US teens can download nudify apps despite Apple and Google controls
content:
A report by the Tech Transparency Project found that U.S. teens can reach “nudify” applications even though Apple and Google offer parental‑control features. Using test accounts presented as 13‑year‑olds, the project downloaded 135 apps that include tools for generating non‑consensual nude imagery.

The report cites a December 2025 incident in Pennsylvania: Morgan Dorfman learned that a student at her daughter’s high school was using an artificial‑intelligence image‑editing app called Movely to produce sexual videos from photographs of her daughter and five other girls. The case illustrates how such apps are being accessed by minors despite existing platform safeguards.
summary: Using test accounts posing as 13‑year‑olds, the Tech Transparency Project downloaded 135 apps that can generate non‑consensual nude imagery. In December 2025, Morgan Dorfman learned that a student at her daughter’s Pennsylvania high school used the AI app Movely to create sexual videos from images of her daughter and five other girls.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Demonstrators block Louvre entrances in Paris on Monday
content: Demonstrators blocked the entrances to the Louvre in Paris on Monday. The action took place as tensions stayed high after a weekend of protests, clashes and looting across France.
summary: Demonstrators blocked the entrances to the Louvre in Paris on Monday. The action occurred as tensions remained high after a weekend of protests, clashes and looting in France.
author: Euronews

title: Qatar prepares new regional defence partnership and warns of imminent energy peak
content: Qatar is preparing a new regional defence partnership and says it will keep diplomatic channels open with Tehran, asserting that dialogue and economic ties can foster lasting peace. Doha also warned that an energy‑disruption “peak” is imminent, with further difficulties expected in the coming days and months.
summary: Qatar is preparing a new regional defence partnership while keeping channels open with Tehran. Doha warned of an energy disruption “peak” that could bring further difficulties in the coming days and months.
author: Euronews

title: Rubio centers Trans‑Caspian trade and critical minerals at C5+1 meeting in Samarkand
content: At a C5+1 meeting in Samarkand, the United States and five Central Asian governments endorsed closer transport and industrial cooperation. U.S. Secretary of State Antony Rubio highlighted Trans‑Caspian trade and critical minerals as central topics of the talks and conducted bilateral discussions. During the same session, Uzbekistan signed the Artemis Accords.
summary: The United States and five Central Asian governments backed closer transport and industrial cooperation at a C5+1 meeting in Samarkand. Rubio held bilateral talks and Uzbekistan signed the Artemis Accords.
author: Euronews

title: French National Rally aims to exploit protests with law‑and‑order rhetoric
content: In the wake of the weekend's violence, the political camps have been trading blame for the “chaos”. The riots have played into the hands of the far-right National Rally, which has been quick to capitalise on the anger and fears over law and order. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell takes a look.
summary: The weekend's violence sparked riots that prompted political camps to trade blame for the chaos. The far‑right National Rally quickly sought to capitalize on anger and fears over law and order.
author: France 24

title: France faces policing scrutiny after violent weekend protests over cost of living
content: France reeled on Monday after a weekend of nationwide unrest sparked by mass protests over the rising cost of living and in support of high‑school students’ demands for education funding. The clashes turned violent, leaving both law‑enforcement officers and protesters wounded, while public buildings were set ablaze and businesses were looted. The scale of the disorder has prompted renewed scrutiny of the French police’s approach to maintaining public order.
summary: France faces policing scrutiny after violent weekend protests over cost of living.
author: France 24

title: AI photos falsely depict elderly couple stripped during France riots
content: AI‑generated images that claim to show an elderly couple “stripped and robbed” amid unrest in France have attracted millions of views. The pictures were amplified by far‑right accounts and have been used to promote inflammatory claims about Muslims, Jews and the riots. FRANCE 24 Observers traced one of the images to an AI photo montage posted by a pro‑Israel account, confirming that the images were created with OpenAI tools. The alleged assault has not been verified, and no official reports confirm that such an attack occurred.
summary: AI-generated photos falsely claiming to show an elderly couple being “stripped and robbed” during unrest in France have racked up millions of views. The images, traced by FRANCE 24 Observers to an AI montage posted by a pro‑Israel account and created with OpenAI tools, remain unverified with no official reports confirming the alleged assault.
author: France 24

title: Le Pen seeks to boost popularity using weekend riots, expert says
content:
After violence erupted over the weekend, political camps have been trading blame for the resulting chaos.  
The riots appear to have benefited the far‑right National Rally, which has quickly capitalised on the anger and fears surrounding law and order.  
Speaking with France 24’s Mark Owen, Dr David Lees, Reader in French Studies at the University of Warwick, said Marine Le Pen is trying to use these events as a vehicle for pushing her popularity ahead of next year’s elections.
summary: The weekend's violence sparked blame between political camps and benefited the far‑right National Rally. Dr David Lees said Marine Le Pen is trying to use the events to push her popularity ahead of next year's elections.
author: France 24

title: France orders Vinted, eBay and Amazon to curb resale of looted items
content: France’s government has asked major second‑hand marketplaces—including Vinted, eBay and Amazon—to crack down on listings that appear to involve stolen goods after weekend violence and looting left thousands of shop owners reeling. The request targets suspicious adverts that have surfaced online.
summary: Thousands of shop owners are reeling from weekend violence and looting, and listings of apparently stolen items have appeared online. France's government asked major second‑hand marketplaces Vinted, eBay and Amazon to crack down on suspicious adverts.
author: France 24

title: Four dead as torrential rain floods eastern Spain, Valencia sees 700 L/m²
content: Torrential rain battered eastern Spain on Monday, causing floodwaters to sweep away cars, submerge roads and strand residents. The flooding killed at least four people in recent days. Emergency crews in Valencia carried out more than 400 rescues, where rainfall reached 700 litres per square metre in 24 hours in some areas.
summary: Torrential rain battered eastern Spain on Monday, killing at least four people as floodwaters swept away cars, submerged roads and stranded residents. Emergency crews carried out more than 400 rescues in Valencia, where rainfall reached 700 litres per square metre in 24 hours in some areas.
author: France 24

title: Korean writer You Yeong-Gwang's debut novel The Rainfall Market a massive success
content: You Yeong‑Gwang’s debut novel, The Rainfall Market, tells the story of a mysterious hidden shop that only opens when it rains. The book achieved massive success despite the author’s unknown status.
summary: You Yeong-Gwang's The Rainfall Market tells the story of a mysterious hidden shop that only opens when it rains. The debut novel by an unknown author was a massive success.
author: DW World

title: Thailand allows Myanmar refugees legal work, first year shows gaps
content: A year after Thailand authorized long‑staying refugees from Myanmar to work legally, the policy has been welcomed by refugees and rights groups. However, those groups note that the program’s first year has revealed significant shortcomings.
summary: A year ago Thailand granted long‑staying refugees from Myanmar the right to work legally. Refugees and rights groups welcomed the move but said the program’s first year exposed significant shortcomings.
author: DW World

title: Rubio visits India, skips New Delhi to tour world's largest oil refinery
content: Washington’s top diplomat, Rubio, will visit India this week, bypassing New Delhi to tour the world’s largest oil refinery. The refinery processes massive amounts of Russian crude. The trip has prompted speculation about whether Trump is seeking a new deal.
summary: Washington's top diplomat Rubio will visit India this week, skipping New Delhi and instead touring the world's largest oil refinery that processes massive amounts of Russian crude. Is Trump looking for a new deal?
author: DW World

title: Ethiopia installs new Tigray administration as Eritrea tensions spark war fears
content:
Ethiopia has installed a new administration in the conflict‑hit region of Tigray after federal forces pushed back Tigrayan fighters.  

Despite this development, tensions with Eritrea persist, raising fears that the conflict could expand into a wider regional war.
summary: Ethiopia has installed a new administration in conflict-hit Tigray after federal forces pushed back Tigrayan fighters. Tensions with Eritrea continue to raise fears of a wider regional war.
author: DW World

title: Canada: Alberta votes on holding independence referendum
content: Alberta is holding a vote on whether to hold an independence referendum. Analysts say the province is not likely to approve a genuine breakaway plebiscite, but the separatist movement hopes the vote will give it leverage over Mark Carney’s government.
summary: Canada's oil-rich western province of Alberta is not deemed likely to vote in favor of a real breakaway plebiscite. Nevertheless the separatist movement hopes to gain leverage over Mark Carney's government.
author: DW World

title: Bulgaria Issues Arrest Warrants for German Nationals Over Starlink Antenna Fires
content: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas and is seeking their detention in Germany. The incident is noted as reminiscent of a similar case in Poland, which Warsaw attributes to Russian orchestration.
summary: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.
author: DW World

title: At least four killed as torrential rain floods eastern Mediterranean coast of Spain
content: At least four people died in Spain after torrential rain battered the country’s eastern Mediterranean coast. The severe flooding left more than 450 people stranded on rooftops, in buildings or in cars.
summary: At least four people have died in Spain as torrential rain battered the eastern Mediterranean coast. The severe flooding left more than 450 people stranded on rooftops, in buildings or in cars.
author: DW World

title: UN biodiversity chief urges urgent action at Yerevan conference
content: At the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, Armenia, the top UN official emphasized that biodiversity losses continue to upend the lives of billions of people. He said future prosperity depends on countries taking urgent action to protect the planet, placing the protection of Earth’s fragile biodiversity in the spotlight.
summary: Biodiversity losses continue to upend the lives of billions of people. The top UN official leading talks at the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan said on Monday that countries need to take urgent action to protect the planet.
author: UN News

title: World Food Programme cuts Gaza food aid, affecting 500,000 as winter nears
content: The United Nations World Food Programme announced on Monday that funding shortages have compelled it to cut food assistance in the Gaza Strip by roughly one‑third. The reduction will leave about 500,000 people without aid as winter approaches.
summary: Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third. The cut will affect about 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.
author: UN News

title: Guterres honors four Indonesian peacekeepers killed in Lebanon
content: UN Secretary-General António Guterres paid tribute to Indonesian peacekeepers on Monday, laying a wreath in honour of four who recently lost their lives in Lebanon and offering a robust defence of UN peacekeeping in what he called “testing times for peace”.
summary: Guterres honors four Indonesian peacekeepers killed in Lebanon.
author: UN News

title: Israeli attacks kill six in Gaza and UN urges protection for West Bank olive farmers
content: Israeli attacks on Gaza over the weekend killed at least six Palestinians, including children, despite a year‑old ceasefire agreement. In the occupied West Bank, settler violence persisted during the olive harvest, prompting UN independent experts on Monday to call on Israel to protect Palestinian farmers.
summary: Israeli attacks on war‑torn Gaza over the weekend killed at least six Palestinians, including children, despite a year‑old ceasefire agreement. UN independent experts on Monday urged Israel to protect Palestinian farmers as settler violence continued during the West Bank olive harvest.
author: UN News

title: Haiti elections paused as gangs adapt to security crackdown, UN tells Security Council
content:
Elections in Haiti remain on hold as gangs adjust to a security crackdown.  

The United Nations told the Security Council on Monday that armed groups are adapting to intensified security operations, stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas.
summary: Elections in Haiti are on hold as gangs adjust to the intensified security crackdown. The UN warned the Security Council on Monday that armed groups are increasing reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas.
author: UN News

title: UN human rights chief Volker Türk calls hunger an avoidable tragedy despite ample food
content: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday that more than a quarter of humanity struggles to obtain enough food even though global production is sufficient for everyone. He described hunger as “an avoidable tragedy” and attributed it to injustice and the denial of human rights.
summary: More than a quarter of humanity struggles to get enough food even though the world produces enough for everyone, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday. He blamed injustice and the denial of human rights for hunger in a world of plenty.
author: UN News

title: Car U-turn hits MP Helen Haines twice in alleged targeted attack
content:
A car allegedly performed a U‑turn before striking Independent MP Helen Haines twice, an incident that some witnesses believe may have been a targeted attack near her electorate office. Police are interviewing the alleged attacker in Wangaratta, Victoria, where the incident occurred.  

Haines was air‑lifted from Wangaratta to Melbourne’s Alfred Hospital for emergency surgery on Monday night. She remains in critical but stable condition following the attack.
summary: A man accused of making a U-turn rammed independent MP Helen Haines's vehicle twice near her electorate office, according to eyewitnesses. Haines was airlifted from Wangaratta to Melbourne's Alfred Hospital, where she remains in critical but stable condition after emergency surgery.
author: Guardian World

title: Barber Ricky Jefferies hailed as hero by PM after intervening in Helen Haines attack
content:
Barber Ricky Jefferies said he had just finished cutting hair when he intervened after a driver allegedly struck independent MP Helen Haines in what police describe as a deliberate attack. According to Jefferies, he grabbed and held the driver at the scene, saying he had “no choice” but to step in.

The Australian prime minister later praised Jefferies as a hero for rushing out of his shop to help Haines. Jefferies was standing outside his barbershop on Tuesday morning; the shop is located next to Haines’ electorate office in Wangaratta. He described himself as “almost shy” about the attention the incident generated.
summary: Ricky Jefferies said he had just finished cutting hair when he grabbed and held the driver who allegedly deliberately struck independent MP Helen Haines. The Australian prime minister hailed Jefferies as a hero for rushing out of his shop to help Haines.
author: Guardian World

title: Independent MP Helen Haines in critical but stable condition after alleged attack
content: A joint counter-terrorism taskforce is investigating the incident, which Anthony Albanese alleged ‘wasn’t an accident’ ‘Deeply appalled’: politicians condemn alleged attack after Helen Haines critically injured Helen Haines, the principled MP respected across parliament ‘It’s very clear that this was a deliberate act’, PM says The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said Haines’ alleged attacker “did a U-turn in order to get back to where Helen Haines was” after passing her on the road. It would appear that the driver of the vehicle that inflicted the damage to Helen Haines did a U-turn in order to get back to where Helen Haines was after passing where she was getting things from the boot or putting things into the boot of her car. So it’s clear that there was a deliberate act here, this wasn’t an accident – someone, you know, just getting off the road here.
summary: Helen Haines, an independent MP, is in critical but stable condition after being struck in an incident that Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said was a deliberate act, not an accident. A joint counter‑terrorism taskforce is investigating the alleged attack.
author: Guardian World

title: Hurricane Trudy weakens to tropical storm after Mexico warnings; one dead in Greece floods
content:
Hurricane Trudy, the 22nd named system of the Pacific season, weakened to a tropical storm after prompting coastal warnings for southwestern Mexico. While the category‑2 hurricane was positioned roughly 100 miles (160 km) southwest of the Mexican coast, the U.S. National Hurricane Center issued hurricane warnings for the coastal portions of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima, forecasting sustained winds of 60‑90 mph on Sunday. Expected rainfall totals of 100‑150 mm raised concerns about flooding, landslides, a dangerous storm surge and damaging waves along the onshore‑wind zones of the region. By Monday morning Trudy had downgraded to a tropical storm and the coastal warnings were lifted.
